5.3.s: pariśrite karoti | brahmavarcasasya parigṛhītyai | na kurvannabhiprāṇyāt | yatkurvannabhiprāṇyāt | prāṇāñchucā'rpayet | apahāya prāṇiti | prāṇānāṃ gopīthāya | na pravargyaṃ cādityaṃ cāntareyāt | yadantareyāt | duścarmā syāt
5.3.d: परिश्रिते करोति । ब्रह्मवर्चसस्य परिगृहीत्यै । न कुर्वन्नभिप्राण्यात् । यत्कुर्वन्नभिप्राण्यात् । प्राणाञ्छुचाऽर्पयेत् । अपहाय प्राणिति । प्राणानां गोपीथाय । न प्रवर्ग्यं चादित्यं चान्तरेयात् । यदन्तरेयात् । दुश्चर्मा स्यात्
5.3.m: He makes it enclosed, for securing brahmic luster. He should not breathe out over it while making it. If he were to breathe out over it while making it, / he would afflict the vital breaths with pain. / Turning away, he breathes out, to protect the vital breaths. He should not go between the pravargya and Āditya. If he were to go between, / he would become skin-diseased.

5.3.s: tasmānnāntarāyyam | ātmano gopīthāya | veṇunā karoti | tejo vai veṇuḥ | tejaḥ pravargyaḥ | tejasaiva tejassamardhayati | makhasya śiro'sītyāha | yajño vai makhaḥ | tasyaitacchiraḥ | yatpravargyaḥ
5.3.d: तस्मान्नान्तराय्यम् । आत्मनो गोपीथाय । वेणुना करोति । तेजो वै वेणुः । तेजः प्रवर्ग्यः । तेजसैव तेजस्समर्धयति । मखस्य शिरोऽसीत्याह । यज्ञो वै मखः । तस्यैतच्छिरः । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः
5.3.m: Therefore, one should not go between them, to protect oneself. He makes it with a bamboo [knife]. Bamboo is indeed fiery energy; / the pravargya is fiery energy. With fiery energy itself he brings fiery energy to perfection. He says, “You are Makha's head.” / Makha is indeed the sacrifice. This is its head, / namely the pravargya.

5.3.s: tasmādevamāha | yajñasya pade stha ityāha | yajñasya hyete pade | atho pratiṣṭhityai | gāyatreṇa tvā chandasā karomītyāha | chandobhirevainaṃ karoti | tryuddhiṃ karoti | traya ime lokāḥ | eṣāṃ lokānāmāptyai | chandobhiḥ karoti
5.3.d: तस्मादेवमाह । यज्ञस्य पदे स्थ इत्याह । यज्ञस्य ह्येते पदे । अथो प्रतिष्ठित्यै । गायत्रेण त्वा छन्दसा करोमीत्याह । छन्दोभिरेवैनं करोति । त्र्युद्धिं करोति । त्रय इमे लोकाः । एषां लोकानामाप्त्यै । छन्दोभिः करोति
5.3.m: Therefore he speaks thus. “You are the two feet of the sacrifice,” he says; for these two are the feet of the sacrifice, and also for firm standing. “I make you with the gāyatrī meter,” he says. / He makes it with the meters themselves. He makes it three tiers high. Three are these worlds; [he does so] to attain these worlds. He makes it with the meters.

5.3.s: vīryaṃ vai chandāṃsi | vīryeṇaivainaṃ karoti | yajuṣā bilaṃ karoti vyāvṛttyai | iyantaṃ karoti | prajāpatinā yajñamukhena saṃmitam | iyantaṃ karoti | yajñaparuṣā saṃmitam | iyantaṃ karoti | etāvadvai puruṣe vīryam | vīryasaṃmitam
5.3.d: वीर्यं वै छन्दांसि । वीर्येणैवैनं करोति । यजुषा बिलं करोति व्यावृत्त्यै । इयन्तं करोति । प्रजापतिना यज्ञमुखेन संमितम् । इयन्तं करोति । यज्ञपरुषा संमितम् । इयन्तं करोति । एतावद्वै पुरुषे वीर्यम् । वीर्यसंमितम्
5.3.m: Vigor indeed are the meters. With vigor itself he makes it. With a yajus he makes the opening, for separation. He makes it this much: / measured by Prajāpati, the mouth of the sacrifice. / He makes it this much: measured by a joint of the sacrifice. He makes it this much: this much indeed is vigor in man; / measured by [that] vigor.

5.3.s: aparimitaṃ karoti | aparimitasyāvaruddhyai | parigrīvaṃ karoti dhṛtyai | sūryasya harasā śrāyetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | aśvaśakena dhūpayati | prājāpatyo vā aśvassayonitvāya | vṛṣṇo aśvasya niṣpadasītyāha | asau vā ādityo vṛṣāśvaḥ | tasya chandāṃsi niṣpat
5.3.d: अपरिमितं करोति । अपरिमितस्यावरुद्ध्यै । परिग्रीवं करोति धृत्यै । सूर्यस्य हरसा श्रायेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । अश्वशकेन धूपयति । प्राजापत्यो वा अश्वस्सयोनित्वाय । वृष्णो अश्वस्य निष्पदसीत्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो वृषाश्वः । तस्य छन्दांसि निष्पत्
5.3.m: He makes it immeasurable, to secure the immeasurable. He makes a neck around it, for stability. “Boil with the heat of Sūrya,” he says; this is just as the yajus [states]. / He fumigates it with horse dung. A horse belongs to Prajāpati; [he does it] for possessing a common origin. “You are the footprint of the stallion,” he says. The stallion horse is that Āditya yonder; his footprint is the meters.

5.3.s: chandobhirevainaṃ dhūpayati | arciṣe tvā śociṣe tvetyāha | teja evāsmindadhāti | vāruṇo'bhīddhaḥ | maitriyopaiti śāntyai | siddhyai tvetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | devastvā savitodvapatvityāha | savitṛprasūta evainaṃ brahmaṇā devatābhirudvapati | apadyamānaḥ pṛthivyāmāśā diśa āpṛṇetyāha
5.3.d: छन्दोभिरेवैनं धूपयति । अर्चिषे त्वा शोचिषे त्वेत्याह । तेज एवास्मिन्दधाति । वारुणोऽभीद्धः । मैत्रियोपैति शान्त्यै । सिद्ध्यै त्वेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । देवस्त्वा सवितोद्वपत्वित्याह । सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं ब्रह्मणा देवताभिरुद्वपति । अपद्यमानः पृथिव्यामाशा दिश आपृणेत्याह
5.3.m: He fumigates it with the meters themselves. “To the flame, to the glowing heat,” he says. He puts fiery energy in it. When it is kindled, it belongs to Varuṇa. He approaches it with [a verse] to Mitra, for peace. “For success, to you,” he says; this is just as the yajus [states]. “May the god Savitṛ unearth you,” he says. / Impelled by Savitṛ, with the brahman, he unearths it with the deities. “Not falling down upon the earth, fill the quarters and spaces,” he says.

5.3.s: tasmādagnissarvā diśo'nuvibhāti | uttiṣṭha bṛhanbhavordhvastiṣṭha dhruvastvamityāha pratiṣṭhityai | īśvaro vā eṣo'ndho bhavitoḥ | yaḥ pravargyamanvīkṣate | sūryasya tvā cakṣuṣā'nvīkṣa ityāha | cakṣuṣo gopīthāya | ṛjave tvā sādhave tvā sukṣityai tvā bhūtyai tvetyāha | iyaṃ vā ṛjuḥ | antarikṣaṃ sādhu | asau sukṣitiḥ
5.3.d: तस्मादग्निस्सर्वा दिशोऽनुविभाति । उत्तिष्ठ बृहन्भवोर्ध्वस्तिष्ठ ध्रुवस्त्वमित्याह प्रतिष्ठित्यै । ईश्वरो वा एषोऽन्धो भवितोः । यः प्रवर्ग्यमन्वीक्षते । सूर्यस्य त्वा चक्षुषाऽन्वीक्ष इत्याह । चक्षुषो गोपीथाय । ऋजवे त्वा साधवे त्वा सुक्षित्यै त्वा भूत्यै त्वेत्याह । इयं वा ऋजुः । अन्तरिक्षं साधु । असौ सुक्षितिः
5.3.m: Therefore, Agni shines forth across all the directions. “Stand up, become great, stand upright, firm are you,” he says, for firm standing. He is indeed liable to become blind / who gazes at the pravargya. “With the eye of Sūrya I gaze at you,” he says, / to protect his eye. “For the straight, for the good, for safe dwelling, for prosperity,” he says. This [earth] is the straight; the intermediate space is the good; that [sky] yonder is safe dwelling;

5.3.s: diśo bhūtiḥ | imānevāsmai lokānkalpayati | atho pratiṣṭhityai | idamahamamumāmuṣyāyaṇaṃ viśā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena paryūhāmītyāha | viśaivainaṃ paśubhirbrahmavarcasena paryūhati | viśeti rājanyasya brūyāt | viśaivainaṃ paryūhati | paśubhiriti vaiśyasya | paśubhirevainaṃ paryūhati | asuryaṃ pātramanācchṛṇṇam
5.3.d: दिशो भूतिः । इमानेवास्मै लोकान्कल्पयति । अथो प्रतिष्ठित्यै । इदमहममुमामुष्यायणं विशा पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पर्यूहामीत्याह । विशैवैनं पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पर्यूहति । विशेति राजन्यस्य ब्रूयात् । विशैवैनं पर्यूहति । पशुभिरिति वैश्यस्य । पशुभिरेवैनं पर्यूहति । असुर्यं पात्रमनाच्छृण्णम्
5.3.m: the directions are prosperity. He establishes these worlds for him, and also for firm standing. / “Here I envelop so-and-so, descendant of so-and-so, with the clan, with cattle, with brahmic luster,” he says. With the clan, with cattle, with brahmic luster he envelops him. “With the clan,” he should say for a rājanya; with the clan alone he envelops him. “With cattle,” for a vaiśya; with cattle alone he envelops him. Unpierced, the vessel belongs to the asuras.

5.3.s: ācchṛṇatti | devatrā'kaḥ | ajakṣīreṇācchṛṇatti | paramaṃ vā etatpayaḥ | yadajakṣīram | parameṇaivainaṃ payasā''cchṛṇatti | yajuṣā vyāvṛttyai | chandobhirācchṛṇatti | chandobhirvā eṣa kriyate | chandobhireva chandāṃsyācchṛṇatti | chṛndhi vācamityāha | vācamevāvarundhe | chṛndhyūrjamityāha | ūrjamevāvarundhe | chṛndhi havirityāha | havirevākaḥ | deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tvetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat
5.3.d: आच्छृणत्ति । देवत्राऽकः । अजक्षीरेणाच्छृणत्ति । परमं वा एतत्पयः । यदजक्षीरम् । परमेणैवैनं पयसा'ऽच्छृणत्ति । यजुषा व्यावृत्त्यै । छन्दोभिराच्छृणत्ति । छन्दोभिर्वा एष क्रियते । छन्दोभिरेव छन्दांस्याच्छृणत्ति । छृन्धि वाचमित्याह । वाचमेवावरुन्धे । छृन्ध्यूर्जमित्याह । ऊर्जमेवावरुन्धे । छृन्धि हविरित्याह । हविरेवाकः । देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत्
5.3.m: He perforates it; he renders it belonging to the gods. He perforates it with goat's milk. This indeed is supreme milk, / namely goat's milk. With supreme milk itself he perforates it; with a yajus, for separation. He perforates it with the meters. With the meters, indeed, this [pot] is made. With the meters themselves he perforates the meters. “Perforate speech,” he says; / he secures speech itself. “Perforate invigorating sap,” he says; he secures invigorating sap itself. “Perforate the oblation,” he says; he makes it an oblation itself. “God, go before; may I reach you,” he says; / this is just as the yajus [states]. / [The anuvāka markers:] He would be, what the pravargya, with the meters he makes, measured by vigor, meters, footprint, fill, he says, safe dwelling, unpierced, the meters he perforates, and eight.

5.4.s: brahmanpracariṣyāmo hotargharmamabhiṣṭuhītyāha | eṣa vā etarhi bṛhaspatiḥ | yadbrahmā | tasmā eva pratiprocya pracarati | ātmano'nārtyai | yamāya tvā makhāya tvetyāha | etā vā etasya devatāḥ | tābhirevainaṃ samardhayati | madantībhiḥ prokṣati | teja evāsmindadhāti
5.4.d: ब्रह्मन्प्रचरिष्यामो होतर्घर्ममभिष्टुहीत्याह । एष वा एतर्हि बृहस्पतिः । यद्ब्रह्मा । तस्मा एव प्रतिप्रोच्य प्रचरति । आत्मनोऽनार्त्यै । यमाय त्वा मखाय त्वेत्याह । एता वा एतस्य देवताः । ताभिरेवैनं समर्धयति । मदन्तीभिः प्रोक्षति । तेज एवास्मिन्दधाति
5.4.m: “O brahman, we shall perform [the rite]; O hotṛ, praise the gharma!” he says. This one is then Bṛhaspati, / namely the brahman [priest]. Having announced it to him, he performs [the rite], / so that he does not suffer injury. “To Yama, to Makha, to you,” he says. These indeed are its deities. / With them he completes it. He sprinkles it with bubbling [waters]; fiery energy itself he bestows upon it.

5.4.s: abhipūrvaṃ prokṣati | abhipūrvamevāsmintejo dadhāti | triḥ prokṣati | tryāvṛddhi yajñaḥ | atho medhyatvāya | hotā'nvāha | rakṣasāmapahatyai | anavānam | prāṇānāṃ santatyai | triṣṭubhassatīrgāyatrīrivānvāha
5.4.d: अभिपूर्वं प्रोक्षति । अभिपूर्वमेवास्मिन्तेजो दधाति । त्रिः प्रोक्षति । त्र्यावृद्धि यज्ञः । अथो मेध्यत्वाय । होताऽन्वाह । रक्षसामपहत्यै । अनवानम् । प्राणानां सन्तत्यै । त्रिष्टुभस्सतीर्गायत्रीरिवान्वाह
5.4.m: He sprinkles it in regular succession; in regular succession he bestows fiery energy upon it. He sprinkles it three times; / threefold is the sacrifice, and also for purity. The hotṛ recites, to smite away the rakṣases, / without catching breath, for the continuation of the vital breaths. Being triṣṭubh [verses], he recites them as if gāyatrīs.

5.4.s: gāyatro hi prāṇaḥ | prāṇameva yajamāne dadhāti | santatamanvāha | prāṇānāmannādyasya santatyai | atho rakṣasāmapahatyai | yatparimitā anubrūyāt | parimitamavarundhīta | aparimitā anvāha | aparimitasyāvaruddhyai | śiro vā etadyajñasya
5.4.d: गायत्रो हि प्राणः । प्राणमेव यजमाने दधाति । सन्ततमन्वाह । प्राणानामन्नाद्यस्य सन्तत्यै । अथो रक्षसामपहत्यै । यत्परिमिता अनुब्रूयात् । परिमितमवरुन्धीत । अपरिमिता अन्वाह । अपरिमितस्यावरुद्ध्यै । शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य
5.4.m: For vital breath is gāyatra. He places vital breath in the sacrificer. He recites continuously, / for the continuation of the vital breaths and food, and also to smite away the rakṣases. If he were to recite a limited number, he would secure what is limited. He recites an unlimited number, to secure the unlimited. A head indeed of this sacrifice

5.4.s: yatpravargyaḥ | ūrṅmuñjāḥ | yanmauñjo vedo bhavati | ūrjaiva yajñasya śirassamardhayati | prāṇāhutīrjuhoti | prāṇāneva yajamāne dadhāti | sapta juhoti | sapta vai śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇāḥ | prāṇānevāsmindadhāti | devastvā savitā madhvā'naktvityāha
5.4.d: यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । ऊर्ङ्मुञ्जाः । यन्मौञ्जो वेदो भवति । ऊर्जैव यज्ञस्य शिरस्समर्धयति । प्राणाहुतीर्जुहोति । प्राणानेव यजमाने दधाति । सप्त जुहोति । सप्त वै शीर्षण्याः प्राणाः । प्राणानेवास्मिन्दधाति । देवस्त्वा सविता मध्वाऽनक्त्वित्याह
5.4.m: is the pravargya. The muñja reeds are invigorating sap. That the grass bundle is made of muñja, / with invigorating sap itself he completes the head of the sacrifice. He offers the breath-oblations. He places vital breaths in the sacrificer. He offers seven; seven indeed are the vital breaths in the head. He places the vital breaths in him. “May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey,” he says.

5.4.s: tejasaivainamanakti | pṛthivīṃ tapasastrāyasveti hiraṇyamupāsyati | asyā anatidāhāya | śiro vā etadyajñasya | yatpravargyaḥ | agnissarvā devatāḥ | pralavānādīpyopāsyati | devatāsveva yajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti | apratiśīrṇāgraṃ bhavati | etadbarhirhyeṣaḥ
5.4.d: तेजसैवैनमनक्ति । पृथिवीं तपसस्त्रायस्वेति हिरण्यमुपास्यति । अस्या अनतिदाहाय । शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । अग्निस्सर्वा देवताः । प्रलवानादीप्योपास्यति । देवतास्वेव यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति । अप्रतिशीर्णाग्रं भवति । एतद्बर्हिर्ह्येषः
5.4.m: With fiery energy alone he anoints him. “Protect the earth from the heat,” [saying this] he throws down a piece of gold, / so that this [earth] is not scorched. A head of the sacrifice is indeed / the pravargya. Agni is all the deities. Having set ablaze the grass trimmings, he casts them down. Among the deities themselves he replaces the head of the sacrifice. It has unbroken tips; for this is the sacrificial grass.

5.4.s: arcirasi śocirasītyāha | teja evāsminbrahmavarcasaṃ dadhāti | saṃsīdasva mahāṃ asītyāha | mahān hyeṣaḥ | brahmavādino vadanti | ete vāva ta ṛtvijaḥ | ye darśapūrṇamāsayoḥ | atha kathā hotā yajamānāyāśiṣo nā''śāsta iti | purastādāśīḥ khalu vā anyo yajñaḥ | upariṣṭādāśīranyaḥ
5.4.d: अर्चिरसि शोचिरसीत्याह । तेज एवास्मिन्ब्रह्मवर्चसं दधाति । संसीदस्व महां असीत्याह । महान् ह्येषः । ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति । एते वाव त ऋत्विजः । ये दर्शपूर्णमासयोः । अथ कथा होता यजमानायाशिषो ना'ऽशास्त इति । पुरस्तादाशीः खलु वा अन्यो यज्ञः । उपरिष्टादाशीरन्यः
5.4.m: "You are the flame, you are the brightness," he says; [thereby] he places brilliance and spiritual pre-eminence in him. "Sit down together, you are great," he says, for he is indeed great. The knowers of brahman say: "These are indeed the very officiating priests who are [present] at the New and Full Moon sacrifices; then why does the Hotṛ not pray for blessings for the sacrificer?" One sacrifice indeed has its blessing in front, another has its blessing at the end.

5.4.s: anādhṛṣyā purastāditi yadetāni yajūgṣyāha | śīrṣata eva yajñasya yajamāna āśiṣo'varundhe | āyuḥ purastādāha | prajāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ | prāṇaṃ paścāt | śrotramuttarataḥ | vidhṛtimupariṣṭāt | prāṇānevāsmai samīco dadhāti | īśvaro vā eṣa diśo'nūnmaditoḥ | yaṃ diśo'nu vyāsthāpayanti
5.4.d: अनाधृष्या पुरस्तादिति यदेतानि यजूग्ष्याह । शीर्षत एव यज्ञस्य यजमान आशिषोऽवरुन्धे । आयुः पुरस्तादाह । प्रजां दक्षिणतः । प्राणं पश्चात् । श्रोत्रमुत्तरतः । विधृतिमुपरिष्टात् । प्राणानेवास्मै समीचो दधाति । ईश्वरो वा एष दिशोऽनून्मदितोः । यं दिशोऽनु व्यास्थापयन्ति
5.4.m: When he utters these formulas, "Unassailable from in front," the sacrificer obtains blessings right from the head of the sacrifice. In front he says, "[May you protect my] lifespan"; on the south, "offspring"; at the rear, "vital breath"; on the north, "hearing"; above, "support." He places the vital breaths in him united. He who is established facing all the directions is liable to go mad after the directions.

5.4.s: manoraśvā'si bhūriputretīmāmabhimṛśati | iyaṃ vai manoraśvā bhūriputtrā | asyāmeva pratitiṣṭhatyanunmādāya | sūpasadā me bhūyā mā mā hiṃsīrityāhāhiṃsāyai | citasstha paricita ityāha | apacitimevāsmindadhāti | śiro vā etadyajñasya | yatpravargyaḥ | asau khalu vā ādityaḥ pravargyaḥ | tasya maruto raśmayaḥ
5.4.d: मनोरश्वाऽसि भूरिपुत्रेतीमामभिमृशति । इयं वै मनोरश्वा भूरिपुत्त्रा । अस्यामेव प्रतितिष्ठत्यनुन्मादाय । सूपसदा मे भूया मा मा हिंसीरित्याहाहिंसायै । चितस्स्थ परिचित इत्याह । अपचितिमेवास्मिन्दधाति । शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । असौ खलु वा आदित्यः प्रवर्ग्यः । तस्य मरुतो रश्मयः
5.4.m: "You are Manu's mare, mother of many sons," [saying this] he touches this [earth]. This [earth] is indeed Manu's mare, mother of many sons. In her he firmly establishes [himself] so as not to go mad. "Be easy of approach for me, do not harm me," he says for the sake of non-harm. "You are piled, you are piled around," he says; he establishes respect in him. The pravargya is indeed the head of this sacrifice. That pravargya is indeed yonder Āditya; the Maruts are his rays.

5.4.s: svāhā marudbhiḥ pariśrayasvetyāha | amumevādityaṃ raśmibhiḥ paryūhati | tasmādasāvādityo'muṣmiṃlloke raśmibhiḥ paryūḍhaḥ | tasmādrājā viśā paryūḍhaḥ | tasmādgrāmaṇīḥ sajātaiḥ paryūḍhaḥ | agneḥ sṛṣṭasya yataḥ | vikaṅkataṃ bhā ārcchat | yadvaikaṅkatāḥ paridhayo bhavanti | bhā evāvarundhe | dvādaśa bhavanti
5.4.d: स्वाहा मरुद्भिः परिश्रयस्वेत्याह । अमुमेवादित्यं रश्मिभिः पर्यूहति । तस्मादसावादित्योऽमुष्मिंल्लोके रश्मिभिः पर्यूढः । तस्माद्राजा विशा पर्यूढः । तस्माद्ग्रामणीः सजातैः पर्यूढः । अग्नेः सृष्टस्य यतः । विकङ्कतं भा आर्च्छत् । यद्वैकङ्कताः परिधयो भवन्ति । भा एवावरुन्धे । द्वादश भवन्ति
5.4.m: "Svāhā! Enclose yourself with the Maruts," he says. He surrounds yonder Āditya with rays. Therefore yonder Āditya is surrounded by rays in yonder world; therefore the king is surrounded by the folk; therefore the village headman is surrounded by his kinsmen. When Agni was emitted, his luster went to the vikaṅkata tree. In that the enclosing sticks are of vikaṅkata wood, he secures luster itself. There are twelve [sticks].

5.4.s: dvādaśa māsāḥ saṃvathsaraḥ | saṃvathsaramevāvarundhe | asti trayodaśo māsa ityāhuḥ | yattrayodaśaḥ paridhirbhavati | tenaiva trayodaśaṃ māsamavarundhe | antarikṣasyāntardhirasītyāha vyāvṛttyai | divaṃ tapasastrāyasvetyupariṣṭāddhiraṇyamadhi nidadhāti | amuṣyā anatidāhāya | atho ābhyāmevainamubhayataḥ parigṛhṇāti | arhanbibharṣi sāyakāni dhanvetyāha
5.4.d: द्वादश मासाः संवथ्सरः । संवथ्सरमेवावरुन्धे । अस्ति त्रयोदशो मास इत्याहुः । यत्त्रयोदशः परिधिर्भवति । तेनैव त्रयोदशं मासमवरुन्धे । अन्तरिक्षस्यान्तर्धिरसीत्याह व्यावृत्त्यै । दिवं तपसस्त्रायस्वेत्युपरिष्टाद्धिरण्यमधि निदधाति । अमुष्या अनतिदाहाय । अथो आभ्यामेवैनमुभयतः परिगृह्णाति । अर्हन्बिभर्षि सायकानि धन्वेत्याह
5.4.m: Twelve months are the year; he secures the year itself. "There is a thirteenth month," they say. In that there is a thirteenth enclosing stick, by that he secures the thirteenth month itself. "You are the partition of the intermediate space," he says, for separation. "Protect the sky from ascetic heat," [saying this] he places gold above, so that she will not be excessively burned. And thus he encompasses him from both sides with these two. "Worthy, you bear arrows and a bow," he says.

5.4.s: stautyevainametat | gāyatramasi traiṣṭubhamasi jāgatamasīti dhavitrāṇyādatte | chandobhirevainānyādatte | madhu madhviti dhūnoti | prāṇo vai madhu | prāṇameva yajamāne dadhāti | triḥ pariyanti | trivṛddhi prāṇaḥ | triḥ pariyanti | tryāvṛddhi yajñaḥ
5.4.d: स्तौत्येवैनमेतत् । गायत्रमसि त्रैष्टुभमसि जागतमसीति धवित्राण्यादत्ते । छन्दोभिरेवैनान्यादत्ते । मधु मध्विति धूनोति । प्राणो वै मधु । प्राणमेव यजमाने दधाति । त्रिः परियन्ति । त्रिवृद्धि प्राणः । त्रिः परियन्ति । त्र्यावृद्धि यज्ञः
5.4.m: He thus praises him. "You are gāyatra, you are traiṣṭubha, you are jāgata," [with these words] he takes the fans; he takes them with the meters itself. "Honey, honey," he fans; honey is indeed vital breath; he places vital breath in the sacrificer. Three times they go around, for threefold is the vital breath. Three times they go around, for threefold is the sacrifice.

5.4.s: atho rakṣasāmapahatyai | triḥ punaḥ pariyanti | ṣaṭth saṃpadyante | ṣaḍvā ṛtavaḥ | ṛtuṣveva pratitiṣṭhanti | yo vai gharmasya priyāṃ tanuvamākrāmati | duścarmā vai sa bhavati | eṣa ha vā asya priyāṃ tanuvamākrāmati | yastriḥ parītya caturthaṃ paryeti | etāṃ ha vā asyogradevo rājanirācakrāma
5.4.d: अथो रक्षसामपहत्यै । त्रिः पुनः परियन्ति । षट्थ् संपद्यन्ते । षड्वा ऋतवः । ऋतुष्वेव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति । यो वै घर्मस्य प्रियां तनुवमाक्रामति । दुश्चर्मा वै स भवति । एष ह वा अस्य प्रियां तनुवमाक्रामति । यस्त्रिः परीत्य चतुर्थं पर्येति । एतां ह वा अस्योग्रदेवो राजनिराचक्राम
5.4.m: Also, [it is] for the repelling of rakṣases. Three times again they go around; they amount to six; six indeed are the seasons; they firmly establish themselves in the seasons. Whoever steps upon the dear body of the gharma, he indeed becomes diseased of skin. He indeed steps upon his dear body who, having gone around three times, goes around a fourth time. Upon this [dear body] Ugradeva, son of Rājani, indeed stepped.

5.4.s: tato vai sa duścarmā'bhavat | tasmāttriḥ parītya na caturthaṃ parīyāt | ātmano gopīthāya | prāṇā vai dhavitrāṇi | avyatiṣaṅgaṃ dhūnvanti | prāṇānāmavyatiṣaṅgāya klṛptyai | viniṣadya dhūnvanti | dikṣveva pratitiṣṭhanti | ūrdhvaṃ dhūnvanti | suvargasya lokasya samaṣṭyai | sarvato dhūnvanti | tasmādayaṃ sarvataḥ pavate
5.4.d: ततो वै स दुश्चर्माऽभवत् । तस्मात्त्रिः परीत्य न चतुर्थं परीयात् । आत्मनो गोपीथाय । प्राणा वै धवित्राणि । अव्यतिषङ्गं धून्वन्ति । प्राणानामव्यतिषङ्गाय क्लृप्त्यै । विनिषद्य धून्वन्ति । दिक्ष्वेव प्रतितिष्ठन्ति । ऊर्ध्वं धून्वन्ति । सुवर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै । सर्वतो धून्वन्ति । तस्मादयं सर्वतः पवते
5.4.m: Then indeed he became diseased of skin; therefore, having gone around three times, one should not go around a fourth time, for the protection of oneself. The fans are vital breaths; they fan without interweaving, for the non-confusion and ordering of the vital breaths. Sitting apart, they fan; they firmly establish themselves in the directions. They fan upwards, for the attainment of the heavenly world. They fan from all sides; therefore this [wind] blows from all sides. He places ... and two [more].

5.5.s: agniṣṭvā vasubhiḥ purastādrocayatu gāyatreṇa chandasetyāha | agnirevainaṃ vasubhiḥ purastādrocayati gāyatreṇa chandasā | sa mā rucito rocayetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | indrastvā rudrairdakṣiṇato rocayatu traiṣṭubhena chandasetyāha | indra evainaṃ rudrairdakṣiṇato rocayati traiṣṭubhena chandasā | sa mā rucito rocayetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | varuṇastvā''dityaiḥ paścādrocayatu jāgatena chandasetyāha | varuṇa evainamādityaiḥ paścādrocayati jāgatena chandasā
5.5.d: अग्निष्ट्वा वसुभिः पुरस्ताद्रोचयतु गायत्रेण छन्दसेत्याह । अग्निरेवैनं वसुभिः पुरस्ताद्रोचयति गायत्रेण छन्दसा । स मा रुचितो रोचयेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । इन्द्रस्त्वा रुद्रैर्दक्षिणतो रोचयतु त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसेत्याह । इन्द्र एवैनं रुद्रैर्दक्षिणतो रोचयति त्रैष्टुभेन छन्दसा । स मा रुचितो रोचयेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । वरुणस्त्वा'ऽदित्यैः पश्चाद्रोचयतु जागतेन छन्दसेत्याह । वरुण एवैनमादित्यैः पश्चाद्रोचयति जागतेन छन्दसा
5.5.m:
"May Agni with the Vasus make you shine from in front with the gāyatrī meter," he says. Agni with the Vasus indeed makes him shine from in front with the gāyatrī meter. "Shone upon, do you make me shine," he says; this blessing he prays for. "May Indra with the Rudras make you shine from the south with the triṣṭubh meter," he says. Indra with the Rudras indeed makes him shine from the south with the triṣṭubh meter. "Shone upon, do you make me shine," he says; this blessing he prays for. "May Varuṇa with the Ādityas make you shine from the rear with the jagatī meter," he says. Varuṇa with the Ādityas indeed makes him shine from the rear with the jagatī meter.

"Shone upon, do you make me shine," he says; this blessing he prays for. "May Dyutāna Māruta with the Maruts make you shine from the north with the anuṣṭubh meter," he says. Dyutāna Māruta with the Maruts indeed makes him shine from the north with the anuṣṭubh meter. "Shone upon, do you make me shine," he says; this blessing he prays for. "May Bṛhaspati with the All-gods make you shine from above with the paṅkti meter," he says. Bṛhaspati with the All-gods indeed makes him shine from above with the paṅkti meter. "Shone upon, do you make me shine," he says; this blessing he prays for.

5.5.s: sa mā rucito rocayetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | dyutānastvā māruto marudbhiruttarato rocayatvānuṣṭubhena chandasetyāha | dyutāna evainaṃ māruto marudbhiruttarato rocayatyānuṣṭubhena chandasā | sa mā rucito rocayetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | bṛhaspatistvā viśvairdevairupariṣṭādrocayatu pāṅktena chandasetyāha | bṛhaspatirevainaṃ viśvairdevairupariṣṭādrocayati pāṅktena chandasā | sa mā rucito rocayetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste
5.5.d: स मा रुचितो रोचयेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । द्युतानस्त्वा मारुतो मरुद्भिरुत्तरतो रोचयत्वानुष्टुभेन छन्दसेत्याह । द्युतान एवैनं मारुतो मरुद्भिरुत्तरतो रोचयत्यानुष्टुभेन छन्दसा । स मा रुचितो रोचयेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । बृहस्पतिस्त्वा विश्वैर्देवैरुपरिष्टाद्रोचयतु पाङ्क्तेन छन्दसेत्याह । बृहस्पतिरेवैनं विश्वैर्देवैरुपरिष्टाद्रोचयति पाङ्क्तेन छन्दसा । स मा रुचितो रोचयेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते

5.5.s: rocitastvaṃ deva gharma deveṣvasītyāha | rocito hyeṣa deveṣu | rociṣīyāhaṃ manuṣyeṣvityāha | rocata evaiṣa manuṣyeṣu | samrāḍgharma rucitastvaṃ deveṣvāyuṣmāṃstejasvī brahmavarcasyasītyāha | rucito hyeṣa deveṣvāyuṣmāṃstejasvī brahmavarcasī | rucito'haṃ manuṣyeṣvāyuṣmāṃstejasvī brahmavarcasī bhūyāsamityāha | rucita evaiṣa manuṣyeṣvāyuṣmāṃstejasvī brahmavarcasī bhavati | rugasi rucaṃ mayi dhehi mayi rugityāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | taṃ yadetairyajurbhirarocayitvā | rucito gharma iti prabrūyāt | arocuko'dhvaryuḥ syāt | arocuko yajamānaḥ | atha yadenametairyajurbhī rocayitvā | rucito gharma iti prāha | rocuko'dhvaryurbhavati | rocuko yajamānaḥ
5.5.d: रोचितस्त्वं देव घर्म देवेष्वसीत्याह । रोचितो ह्येष देवेषु । रोचिषीयाहं मनुष्येष्वित्याह । रोचत एवैष मनुष्येषु । सम्राड्घर्म रुचितस्त्वं देवेष्वायुष्मांस्तेजस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चस्यसीत्याह । रुचितो ह्येष देवेष्वायुष्मांस्तेजस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी । रुचितोऽहं मनुष्येष्वायुष्मांस्तेजस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी भूयासमित्याह । रुचित एवैष मनुष्येष्वायुष्मांस्तेजस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति । रुगसि रुचं मयि धेहि मयि रुगित्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । तं यदेतैर्यजुर्भिररोचयित्वा । रुचितो घर्म इति प्रब्रूयात् । अरोचुकोऽध्वर्युः स्यात् । अरोचुको यजमानः । अथ यदेनमेतैर्यजुर्भी रोचयित्वा । रुचितो घर्म इति प्राह । रोचुकोऽध्वर्युर्भवति । रोचुको यजमानः
5.5.m: "Made to shine, O divine gharma, you are among the gods," he says, for he is made to shine among the gods. "May I shine among men," he says; he shines among men. "O sovereign gharma, shone upon, you are endowed with lifespan, brilliant, and endowed with spiritual pre-eminence among the gods," he says, for he is shone upon, endowed with lifespan, brilliant, and endowed with spiritual pre-eminence among the gods. "Shone upon, may I become endowed with lifespan, brilliant, and endowed with spiritual pre-eminence among men," he says; shone upon, he becomes endowed with lifespan, brilliant, and endowed with spiritual pre-eminence among men. "You are light, place light in me, light is in me," he says; this blessing he prays for. If, without having made it shine with these formulas, he should say, "The gharma is shone upon," the Adhvaryu would become lusterless, the sacrificer lusterless. But when, having made it shine with these formulas, he says, "The gharma is shone upon," the Adhvaryu becomes luminous, the sacrificer luminous. Makes shine from the rear with the jagatī meter ... and eight [more].

5.6.s: śiro vā etadyajñasya | yatpravargyaḥ | grīvā upasadaḥ | purastādupasadāṃ pravargyaṃ pravṛṇakti | grīvāsveva yajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti | triḥ pravṛṇakti | traya ime lokāḥ | ebhya eva lokebhyo yajñasya śiro'varundhe | ṣaṭth saṃpadyante | ṣaḍvā ṛtavaḥ
5.6.d: शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । ग्रीवा उपसदः । पुरस्तादुपसदां प्रवर्ग्यं प्रवृणक्ति । ग्रीवास्वेव यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति । त्रिः प्रवृणक्ति । त्रय इमे लोकाः । एभ्य एव लोकेभ्यो यज्ञस्य शिरोऽवरुन्धे । षट्थ् संपद्यन्ते । षड्वा ऋतवः
5.6.m: The pravargya is indeed the head of this sacrifice; the upasads are the neck. He performs the pravargya before the upasads; he places the head of the sacrifice on the neck itself. Three times he performs it; three are these worlds; from these worlds he secures the head of the sacrifice. They amount to six; six indeed are the seasons.

5.6.s: ṛtubhya eva yajñasya śiro'varundhe | dvādaśakṛtvaḥ pravṛṇakti | dvādaśa māsāssaṃvathsaraḥ | saṃvathsarādeva yajñasya śiro'varundhe | caturviṃśatissaṃpadyante | caturviṃśatirardhamāsāḥ | ardhamāsebhya eva yajñasya śiro'varundhe | atho khalu | sakṛdeva pravṛjyaḥ | ekaṃ hi śiraḥ
5.6.d: ऋतुभ्य एव यज्ञस्य शिरोऽवरुन्धे । द्वादशकृत्वः प्रवृणक्ति । द्वादश मासास्संवथ्सरः । संवथ्सरादेव यज्ञस्य शिरोऽवरुन्धे । चतुर्विंशतिस्संपद्यन्ते । चतुर्विंशतिरर्धमासाः । अर्धमासेभ्य एव यज्ञस्य शिरोऽवरुन्धे । अथो खलु । सकृदेव प्रवृज्यः । एकं हि शिरः
5.6.m: From the seasons indeed he secures the head of the sacrifice. Twelve times he performs the pravargya. Twelve months are a year; from the year indeed he secures the head of the sacrifice. Twenty-four they amount to; twenty-four are the half-months; from the half-months indeed he secures the head of the sacrifice. And then indeed, it is to be performed only once, for single is the head.

5.6.s: agniṣṭome pravṛṇakti | etāvān vai yajñaḥ | yāvānagniṣṭomaḥ | yāvāneva yajñaḥ | tasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti | nokthye pravṛñjyāt | prajā vai paśava ukthāni | yadukthye pravṛñjyāt | prajāṃ paśūnasya nirdahet | viśvajiti sarvapṛṣṭhe pravṛṇakti
5.6.d: अग्निष्टोमे प्रवृणक्ति । एतावान् वै यज्ञः । यावानग्निष्टोमः । यावानेव यज्ञः । तस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति । नोक्थ्ये प्रवृञ्ज्यात् । प्रजा वै पशव उक्थानि । यदुक्थ्ये प्रवृञ्ज्यात् । प्रजां पशूनस्य निर्दहेत् । विश्वजिति सर्वपृष्ठे प्रवृणक्ति
5.6.m: At the Agniṣṭoma he performs the pravargya. As great indeed as the sacrifice is, so great is the Agniṣṭoma. As great as the sacrifice is, of that he puts together the head. He should not perform it at the Ukthya. Offspring indeed and cattle are the ukthas; if he should perform it at the Ukthya, he would burn up his offspring and cattle. At the Viśvajit Sarvapṛṣṭha he performs the pravargya.

5.6.s: pṛṣṭhāni vā acyutaṃ cyāvayanti | pṛṣṭhairevāsmā acyutaṃ cyāvayitvā'varundhe | apaśyaṃ gopāmityāha | prāṇo vai gopāḥ | prāṇameva prajāsu viyātayati | apaśyaṃ gopāmityāha | asau vā ādityo gopāḥ | sa hīmāḥ prajā gopāyati | tameva prajānāṃ goptāraṃ kurute | anipadyamānamityāha
5.6.d: पृष्ठानि वा अच्युतं च्यावयन्ति । पृष्ठैरेवास्मा अच्युतं च्यावयित्वाऽवरुन्धे । अपश्यं गोपामित्याह । प्राणो वै गोपाः । प्राणमेव प्रजासु वियातयति । अपश्यं गोपामित्याह । असौ वा आदित्यो गोपाः । स हीमाः प्रजा गोपायति । तमेव प्रजानां गोप्तारं कुरुते । अनिपद्यमानमित्याह
5.6.m: The pṛṣṭhas indeed shake the unshakable; by means of the pṛṣṭhas he shakes the unshakable for him and secures it. “I saw the herdsman,” he says. The vital breath indeed is the herdsman; he distributes the vital breath among offspring. “I saw the herdsman,” he says. That Āditya indeed is the herdsman, for he guards these creatures; he makes him the guardian of offspring. “Unresting,” he says.

5.6.s: na hyeṣa nipadyate | ā ca parā ca pathibhiścarantamityāha | ā ca hyeṣa parā ca pathibhiścarati | sa saddhrīcīssa viṣūcīrvasāna ityāha | saddhrīcīśca hyeṣa viṣūcīśca vasānaḥ prajā abhivipaśyati | āvarīvarti bhuvaneṣvantarityāha | ā hyeṣa varīvarti bhuvaneṣvantaḥ | atra prāvīrmadhumādhvībhyāṃ madhumādhūcībhyāmityāha | vāsantikāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati | samagniragninā gatetyāha
5.6.d: न ह्येष निपद्यते । आ च परा च पथिभिश्चरन्तमित्याह । आ च ह्येष परा च पथिभिश्चरति । स सद्ध्रीचीस्स विषूचीर्वसान इत्याह । सद्ध्रीचीश्च ह्येष विषूचीश्च वसानः प्रजा अभिविपश्यति । आवरीवर्ति भुवनेष्वन्तरित्याह । आ ह्येष वरीवर्ति भुवनेष्वन्तः । अत्र प्रावीर्मधुमाध्वीभ्यां मधुमाधूचीभ्यामित्याह । वासन्तिकावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति । समग्निरग्निना गतेत्याह
5.6.m: For he does not rest. “Wandering here and there along the paths,” he says; for he wanders here and there along the paths. “Clothed in converging and diverging [rays],” he says; for clothed in converging and diverging [rays], he looks down upon creatures. “He revolves continually within the worlds,” he says; for he continually revolves within the worlds. “Here protect with the two sweet, honey-bearing ones,” he says; he arranges for him the two seasons of spring. “Agni has united with Agni,” he says.

5.6.s: graiṣmāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati | samagniragninā gatetyāha | agnirhyevaiṣo'gninā saṃgacchate | svāhā samagnistapasā gatetyāha | pūrvamevoditam | uttareṇābhigṛṇāti | dhartā divo vibhāsi rajasaḥ pṛthivyā ityāha | vārṣikāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati | hṛde tvā manase tvetyāha | śāradāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati
5.6.d: ग्रैष्मावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति । समग्निरग्निना गतेत्याह । अग्निर्ह्येवैषोऽग्निना संगच्छते । स्वाहा समग्निस्तपसा गतेत्याह । पूर्वमेवोदितम् । उत्तरेणाभिगृणाति । धर्ता दिवो विभासि रजसः पृथिव्या इत्याह । वार्षिकावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति । हृदे त्वा मनसे त्वेत्याह । शारदावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति
5.6.m: He arranges for him the two seasons of summer. “Agni has united with Agni,” he says, for Agni indeed unites with Agni. “Svāhā, Agni has united with ascetic heat,” he says; what was said before, he follows up with the latter. “Maintainer of the sky, you shine over the realm of earth,” he says; he arranges for him the two seasons of the rains. “For the heart, for the mind, [I take] you,” he says; he arranges for him the two seasons of autumn.

5.6.s: divi deveṣu hotrā yacchetyāha | hotrābhirevemān lokānthsaṃdadhāti | viśvāsāṃ bhuvāṃ pata ityāha | haimantikāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati | devaśrūstvaṃ deva gharma devānpāhītyāha | śaiśirāvevāsmā ṛtū kalpayati | tapojāṃ vācamasme niyaccha devāyuvamityāha | yā vai medhyā vāk | sā tapojāḥ | tāmevāvarundhe
5.6.d: दिवि देवेषु होत्रा यच्छेत्याह । होत्राभिरेवेमान् लोकान्थ्संदधाति । विश्वासां भुवां पत इत्याह । हैमन्तिकावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति । देवश्रूस्त्वं देव घर्म देवान्पाहीत्याह । शैशिरावेवास्मा ऋतू कल्पयति । तपोजां वाचमस्मे नियच्छ देवायुवमित्याह । या वै मेध्या वाक् । सा तपोजाः । तामेवावरुन्धे
5.6.m: “In the sky among the gods, extend the invocations,” he says; by means of the invocations he joins these worlds together. “O lord of all beings,” he says; he arranges for him the two seasons of winter. “Hearing the gods, divine gharma, protect the gods,” he says; he arranges for him the two seasons of the cool season. “Bestow on us speech born of ascetic heat, seeking the gods,” he says. That speech which is sacrificial, that is born of ascetic heat; that indeed he secures.

5.6.s: garbho devānāmityāha | garbho hyeṣa devānām | pitā matīnāmityāha | prajā vai matayaḥ | tāsāmeṣa eva pitā | yatpravargyaḥ | tasmādevamāha | patiḥ prajānāmityāha | patirhyeṣa prajānām | matiḥ kavīnāmityāha
5.6.d: गर्भो देवानामित्याह । गर्भो ह्येष देवानाम् । पिता मतीनामित्याह । प्रजा वै मतयः । तासामेष एव पिता । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । तस्मादेवमाह । पतिः प्रजानामित्याह । पतिर्ह्येष प्रजानाम् । मतिः कवीनामित्याह
5.6.m: “Embryo of the gods,” he says; for he is the embryo of the gods. “Father of thoughts,” he says. Offspring indeed are thoughts; of them he is the father, which is the pravargya; therefore he speaks thus. “Lord of creatures,” he says; for he is the lord of creatures. “Thought of the wise,” he says.

5.6.s: matirhyeṣa kavīnām | saṃ devo devena savitrā'yatiṣṭa saṃ sūryeṇāruktetyāha | amuṃ caivādityaṃ pravargyaṃ ca saṃ śāsti | āyurdāstvamasmabhyaṃ gharma varcodā asītyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | pitā no'si pitā no bodhetyāha | bodhayatyevainam | navaite'vakāśā bhavanti | patniyai daśamaḥ | nava vai puruṣe prāṇāḥ
5.6.d: मतिर्ह्येष कवीनाम् । सं देवो देवेन सवित्राऽयतिष्ट सं सूर्येणारुक्तेत्याह । अमुं चैवादित्यं प्रवर्ग्यं च सं शास्ति । आयुर्दास्त्वमस्मभ्यं घर्म वर्चोदा असीत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । पिता नोऽसि पिता नो बोधेत्याह । बोधयत्येवैनम् । नवैतेऽवकाशा भवन्ति । पत्नियै दशमः । नव वै पुरुषे प्राणाः
5.6.m: For he is the thought of the wise. “The god has united with the god Savitṛ, he has shone forth with Sūrya,” he says; he harmonizes both that Āditya and the pravargya. “Giver of lifespan are you to us, O gharma, giver of luster are you,” he says; this blessing indeed he invokes. “You are our father; recognize us as a father,” he says; he awakens him indeed. Nine are these intermediate spaces; the tenth is for the wife. Nine indeed are the vital breaths in a man.

5.6.s: nābhirdaśamī | prāṇāneva yajamāne dadhāti | atho daśākṣarā virāṭ | annaṃ virāṭ | virājaivānnādyamavarundhe | yajñasya śiro'cchidyata | taddevā hotrābhiḥ pratyadadhuḥ | ṛtvijo'vekṣante | etā vai hotrāḥ | hotrābhireva yajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti
5.6.d: नाभिर्दशमी । प्राणानेव यजमाने दधाति । अथो दशाक्षरा विराट् । अन्नं विराट् । विराजैवान्नाद्यमवरुन्धे । यज्ञस्य शिरोऽच्छिद्यत । तद्देवा होत्राभिः प्रत्यदधुः । ऋत्विजोऽवेक्षन्ते । एता वै होत्राः । होत्राभिरेव यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति
5.6.m: The navel is the tenth. He places the vital breaths in the sacrificer. Moreover, the virāj has ten syllables; food is the virāj; by means of the virāj he secures proper food. The head of the sacrifice was cut off; that the gods restored with the invocations. The priests look on; these are the invocations; with the invocations indeed he restores the head of the sacrifice.

5.6.s: rucitamavekṣante | rucitādvai prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata | prajānāṃ sṛṣṭyai | rucitamavekṣante | rucitādvai parjanyo varṣati | varṣukaḥ parjanyo bhavati | saṃ prajā edhante | rucitamavekṣante | rucitaṃ vai brahmavarcasam | brahmavarcasino bhavanti
5.6.d: रुचितमवेक्षन्ते । रुचिताद्वै प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत । प्रजानां सृष्ट्यै । रुचितमवेक्षन्ते । रुचिताद्वै पर्जन्यो वर्षति । वर्षुकः पर्जन्यो भवति । सं प्रजा एधन्ते । रुचितमवेक्षन्ते । रुचितं वै ब्रह्मवर्चसम् । ब्रह्मवर्चसिनो भवन्ति
5.6.m: They look at what is brightened. From what was brightened, Prajāpati created offspring, for the procreation of offspring. They look at what is brightened. From what is brightened, Parjanya rains; Parjanya becomes prone to rain; creatures thrive. They look at what is brightened. What is brightened is spiritual luster; they become endowed with spiritual luster.

5.6.s: adhīyanto'vekṣante | sarvamāyuryanti | na patnyavekṣeta | yatpatnyavekṣeta | prajāyeta | prajāṃ tvasyai nirdahet | yannāvekṣeta | na prajāyeta | nāsyai prajāṃ nirdahet | tiraskṛtya yajurvācayati | prajāyate | nāsyai prajāṃ nirdahati | tvaṣṭīmatī te sapeyetyāha | sapāddhi prajāḥ prajāyante
5.6.d: अधीयन्तोऽवेक्षन्ते । सर्वमायुर्यन्ति । न पत्न्यवेक्षेत । यत्पत्न्यवेक्षेत । प्रजायेत । प्रजां त्वस्यै निर्दहेत् । यन्नावेक्षेत । न प्रजायेत । नास्यै प्रजां निर्दहेत् । तिरस्कृत्य यजुर्वाचयति । प्रजायते । नास्यै प्रजां निर्दहति । त्वष्टीमती ते सपेयेत्याह । सपाद्धि प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते
5.6.m: Repeating [the mantras], they look; they attain full lifespan. The wife should not look. If the wife were to look, she would produce offspring, but he would burn up her offspring. If she were not to look, she would not produce offspring, and he would not burn up her offspring. Having covered [her eyes], he makes her recite the yajus formula; she produces offspring, and he does not burn up her offspring. “May I unite with you, who are accompanied by Tvaṣṭṛ,” he says; for from union offspring are born. / The seasons indeed are the head / at the Sarvapṛṣṭha he performs / “Unresting,” he says / “united,” he says / he arranges for him the two seasons of autumn / he secures / “of the wise,” he says / the vital breaths / he puts together / they become / he makes recite, and four.

5.7.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava iti raśanāmādatte prasūtyai | aśvinorbāhubhyāmityāha | aśvinau hi devānāmadhvaryū āstām | pūṣṇo hastābhyāmityāha yatyai | ādade'dityai rāsnā'sītyāha yajuṣkṛtyai | iḍa ehyadita ehi sarasvatyehītyāha | etāni vā asyai devanāmāni | devanāmairevaināmāhvayati | asāvehyasāvehyasāvehītyāha | etāni vā asyai manuṣyanāmāni
5.7.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इति रशनामादत्ते प्रसूत्यै । अश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यामित्याह । अश्विनौ हि देवानामध्वर्यू आस्ताम् । पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यामित्याह यत्यै । आददेऽदित्यै रास्नाऽसीत्याह यजुष्कृत्यै । इड एह्यदित एहि सरस्वत्येहीत्याह । एतानि वा अस्यै देवनामानि । देवनामैरेवैनामाह्वयति । असावेह्यसावेह्यसावेहीत्याह । एतानि वा अस्यै मनुष्यनामानि
5.7.m: “At the impulse of the god Savitṛ,” he takes the rope for impelling. “With the arms of the Aśvins,” he says; for the two Aśvins were the adhvaryu priests of the gods. “With the hands of Pūṣan,” he says, for restraining. “I take [you]; you are the girdle of Aditi,” he says, to make it a yajus formula. “Come, Iḍā; come, Aditi; come, Sarasvatī,” he says; these indeed are her divine names; with the divine names he summons her. “Come, so-and-so; come, so-and-so; come, so-and-so,” he says; these indeed are her human names.

5.7.s: manuṣyanāmairevaināmāhvayati | ṣaṭtha saṃpadyante | ṣaḍvā ṛtavaḥ | ṛtubhirevaināmāhvayati | adityā uṣṇīṣamasītyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | vāyurasyaiḍa ityāha | vāyudevatyo vai vathsaḥ | pūṣā tvopāvasṛjatvityāha | pauṣṇā vai devatayā paśavaḥ
5.7.d: मनुष्यनामैरेवैनामाह्वयति । षट्थ संपद्यन्ते । षड्वा ऋतवः । ऋतुभिरेवैनामाह्वयति । अदित्या उष्णीषमसीत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । वायुरस्यैड इत्याह । वायुदेवत्यो वै वथ्सः । पूषा त्वोपावसृजत्वित्याह । पौष्णा वै देवतया पशवः
5.7.m: With the human names he summons her. Six they amount to; six are the seasons; with the seasons he summons her. “You are the turban of Aditi,” he says; this is just as the yajus formula [says]. “You are Vāyu belonging to Iḍā,” he says; the calf has Vāyu as its deity. “May Pūṣan release you,” he says; cattle belong to the deity Pūṣan.

5.7.s: svayaivainaṃ devatayopāvasṛjati | aśvibhyāṃ pradāpayetyāha | aśvinau vai devānāṃ bhiṣajau | tābhyāmevāsmai bheṣajaṃ karoti | yaste stanaḥ śaśaya ityāha | stautyevainām | usra gharmaṃ śiṃṣosra gharmaṃ pāhi gharmāya śiṃṣetyāha | yathā brūyādamuṣmai dehīti | tādṛgeva tat | bṛhaspatistvopasīdatvityāha
5.7.d: स्वयैवैनं देवतयोपावसृजति । अश्विभ्यां प्रदापयेत्याह । अश्विनौ वै देवानां भिषजौ । ताभ्यामेवास्मै भेषजं करोति । यस्ते स्तनः शशय इत्याह । स्तौत्येवैनाम् । उस्र घर्मं शिंषोस्र घर्मं पाहि घर्माय शिंषेत्याह । यथा ब्रूयादमुष्मै देहीति । तादृगेव तत् । बृहस्पतिस्त्वोपसीदत्वित्याह
5.7.m: With his own deity he releases him. “Make [her] yield for the Aśvins,” he says; the Aśvins are the physicians of the gods; for him he makes medicine through both of them. “That udder of yours which rests,” he says; he praises her indeed. “O cow, leave over for the gharma; O cow, protect the gharma; leave over for the gharma,” he says; just as one would say, “Give to such a one,” such indeed is that. “May Bṛhaspati sit beside you,” he says.

5.7.s: brahma vai devānāṃ bṛhaspatiḥ | brahmaṇaivaināmupasīdati | dānavasstha perava ityāha | medhyānevainānkaroti | viṣvagvṛto lohitenetyāha vyāvṛtyai | aśvibhyāṃ pinvasva sarasvatyai pinvasva pūṣṇe pinvasva bṛhaspataye pinvasvetyāha | etābhyo hyeṣā devatābhyaḥ pinvate | indrāya pinvasvendrāya pinvasvetyāha | indrameva bhāgadheyena samardhayati | dvirindrāyetyāha
5.7.d: ब्रह्म वै देवानां बृहस्पतिः । ब्रह्मणैवैनामुपसीदति । दानवस्स्थ पेरव इत्याह । मेध्यानेवैनान्करोति । विष्वग्वृतो लोहितेनेत्याह व्यावृत्यै । अश्विभ्यां पिन्वस्व सरस्वत्यै पिन्वस्व पूष्णे पिन्वस्व बृहस्पतये पिन्वस्वेत्याह । एताभ्यो ह्येषा देवताभ्यः पिन्वते । इन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेन्द्राय पिन्वस्वेत्याह । इन्द्रमेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति । द्विरिन्द्रायेत्याह
5.7.m: Brahman among the gods is Bṛhaspati; through brahman he sits beside her. “You are the generous ones, the nourishing ones,” he says; he makes them sacrificial. “Surrounded on all sides with blood,” he says, for separation. “Swell for the Aśvins, swell for Sarasvatī, swell for Pūṣan, swell for Bṛhaspati,” he says; for these deities indeed she swells. “Swell for Indra, swell for Indra,” he says; he enriches Indra with his share. Twice he says, “For Indra.”

5.7.s: tasmādindro devatānāṃ bhūyiṣṭhabhāktamaḥ | gāyatro'si traiṣṭubho'si jāgatamasīti śaphopayamānādatte | chandobhirevainānādatte | sahorjo bhāgenopamehītyāha | ūrja evainaṃ bhāgamakaḥ | aśvinau vā etadyajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhatāvabrūtām | āvābhyāmeva pūrvābhyāṃ vaṣaṭkriyātā iti | indrāśvinā madhunassāraghasyetyāha | aśvibhyāmeva pūrvābhyāṃ vaṣaṭkaroti | atho aśvināveva bhāgadheyena samardhayati
5.7.d: तस्मादिन्द्रो देवतानां भूयिष्ठभाक्तमः । गायत्रोऽसि त्रैष्टुभोऽसि जागतमसीति शफोपयमानादत्ते । छन्दोभिरेवैनानादत्ते । सहोर्जो भागेनोपमेहीत्याह । ऊर्ज एवैनं भागमकः । अश्विनौ वा एतद्यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधतावब्रूताम् । आवाभ्यामेव पूर्वाभ्यां वषट्क्रियाता इति । इन्द्राश्विना मधुनस्सारघस्येत्याह । अश्विभ्यामेव पूर्वाभ्यां वषट्करोति । अथो अश्विनावेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति
5.7.m: Therefore Indra receives the greatest portion among the gods. Saying, "You are of the gāyatrī metre, you are of the triṣṭubh metre, you are of the jagatī metre," he takes the pair of tongs. He takes them indeed with the metres. He says, "Come to me with a share of invigorating food." He has indeed made invigorating food his portion. When the two Aśvins were putting the head of the sacrifice back together, they said, "Let the vaṣaṭ-call be made for us two first." He says, "O Indra and Aśvins, of the sweet honey produced by bees." He makes the vaṣaṭ-call for the Aśvins first. Thus he also enriches the two Aśvins with their portion.

5.7.s: gharmaṃ pāta vasavo yajatā vaḍityāha | vasūneva bhāgadheyena samardhayati | yadvaṣaṭkuryāt | yātayāmā'sya vaṣaṭkārassyāt | yanna vaṣaṭkuryāt | rakṣāṃsi yajñaṃ hanyuḥ | vaḍityāha | parokṣameva vaṣaṭkaroti | nāsya yātayāmā vaṣaṭkāro bhavati | na yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsi ghnanti
5.7.d: घर्मं पात वसवो यजता वडित्याह । वसूनेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति । यद्वषट्कुर्यात् । यातयामाऽस्य वषट्कारस्स्यात् । यन्न वषट्कुर्यात् । रक्षांसि यज्ञं हन्युः । वडित्याह । परोक्षमेव वषट्करोति । नास्य यातयामा वषट्कारो भवति । न यज्ञं रक्षांसि घ्नन्ति
5.7.m: He says, "Drink the gharma, O worshipful Vasus, vaṭ!" He enriches the Vasus with their portion. If he should make the vaṣaṭ-call, his vaṣaṭ-call would become stale. If he should not make the vaṣaṭ-call, the rakṣases would destroy the sacrifice. He says, "Vaṭ!" He makes the vaṣaṭ-call cryptically. His vaṣaṭ-call does not become stale; the rakṣases do not destroy the sacrifice.

5.7.s: svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmaye vṛṣṭivanaye juhomītyāha | yo vā asya puṇyo raśmiḥ | sa vṛṣṭivaniḥ | tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | madhu havirasītyāha | svadayatyevainam | sūryasya tapastapetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tvā parigṛhṇāmītyāha | dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmevainaṃ parigṛhṇāti
5.7.d: स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मये वृष्टिवनये जुहोमीत्याह । यो वा अस्य पुण्यो रश्मिः । स वृष्टिवनिः । तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । मधु हविरसीत्याह । स्वदयत्येवैनम् । सूर्यस्य तपस्तपेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां त्वा परिगृह्णामीत्याह । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामेवैनं परिगृह्णाति
5.7.m: He says, "Svāhā! I offer you to the ray of Sūrya that wins the rain." That auspicious ray of his is the one that wins rain; to it he offers this. He says, "You are sweet oblation." He thus sweetens it. He says, "Glow with the heat of Sūrya!" This is just according to the yajus. He says, "I take hold of you with sky and earth." He takes hold of it with sky and earth.

5.7.s: antarikṣeṇa tvopayacchāmītyāha | antarikṣeṇaivainamupayacchati | na vā etaṃ manuṣyo bhartumarhati | devānāṃ tvā pitṛṇāmanumato bhartuṃ śakeyamityāha | devairevainaṃ pitṛbhiranumata ādatte | vi vā enametadardhayanti | yatpaścātpravṛjya puro juhvati | tejo'si tejo'nuprehītyāha | teja evāsmindadhāti | divispṛṅmā mā hiṃsīrantarikṣaspṛṅmā mā hiṃsīḥ pṛthivispṛṅmā mā hiṃsīrityāhāhiṃsāyai
5.7.d: अन्तरिक्षेण त्वोपयच्छामीत्याह । अन्तरिक्षेणैवैनमुपयच्छति । न वा एतं मनुष्यो भर्तुमर्हति । देवानां त्वा पितृणामनुमतो भर्तुं शकेयमित्याह । देवैरेवैनं पितृभिरनुमत आदत्ते । वि वा एनमेतदर्धयन्ति । यत्पश्चात्प्रवृज्य पुरो जुह्वति । तेजोऽसि तेजोऽनुप्रेहीत्याह । तेज एवास्मिन्दधाति । दिविस्पृङ्मा मा हिंसीरन्तरिक्षस्पृङ्मा मा हिंसीः पृथिविस्पृङ्मा मा हिंसीरित्याहाहिंसायै
5.7.m: He says, "I support you with the intermediate space." He supports it with the intermediate space. No human being is capable of bearing this. He says, "Approved by the gods, by the fathers, may I be able to bear you." Approved by the gods and by the fathers, he takes it. They indeed halve it when, having placed it on the fire in the west, they offer it in the east. He says, "You are splendour; go after splendour." He places splendour in it. He says, "Touching the sky, do not harm me; touching the intermediate space, do not harm me; touching the earth, do not harm me," for the sake of non-harming.

5.7.s: suvarasi suvarme yaccha divaṃ yaccha divo mā pāhītyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | śiro vā etadyajñasya | yatpravargyaḥ | ātmā vāyuḥ | udyatyavātanāmānyāha | ātmanneva yajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti | anavānam | prāṇānāṃ saṃtatyai | pañcāha
5.7.d: सुवरसि सुवर्मे यच्छ दिवं यच्छ दिवो मा पाहीत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । आत्मा वायुः । उद्यत्यवातनामान्याह । आत्मन्नेव यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति । अनवानम् । प्राणानां संतत्यै । पञ्चाह
5.7.m: He says, "You are heaven; grant me heaven; grant the sky; protect me from the sky." He thus prays for this blessing. The pravargya is indeed the head of the sacrifice; Vāyu is the breath. While raising it, he recites the names of the winds. He places the head of the sacrifice back upon its breath, without drawing breath, for the continuity of the vital breaths. He recites five.

5.7.s: pāṅkto yajñaḥ | yāvāneva yajñaḥ | tasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti | agnaye tvā vasumate svāhetyāha | asau vā ādityo'gnirvasumān | tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | somāya tvā rudravate svāhetyāha | candramā vai somo rudravān | tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | varuṇāya tvā''dityavate svāhetyāha
5.7.d: पाङ्क्तो यज्ञः । यावानेव यज्ञः । तस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति । अग्नये त्वा वसुमते स्वाहेत्याह । असौ वा आदित्योऽग्निर्वसुमान् । तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । सोमाय त्वा रुद्रवते स्वाहेत्याह । चन्द्रमा वै सोमो रुद्रवान् । तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । वरुणाय त्वा'ऽदित्यवते स्वाहेत्याह
5.7.m: The sacrifice is fivefold. As great as the sacrifice is, he puts back its head. He says, "To Agni accompanied by the Vasus, svāhā!" Yonder Āditya is Agni accompanied by the Vasus; to him he offers it. He says, "To Soma accompanied by the Rudras, svāhā!" The moon is Soma accompanied by the Rudras; to him he offers it. He says, "To Varuṇa accompanied by the Ādityas, svāhā!"

5.7.s: apsu vai varuṇa ādityavān | tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | bṛhaspataye tvā viśvadevyāvate svāhetyāha | brahma vai devānāṃ bṛhaspatiḥ | brahmaṇa evainaṃ juhoti | savitre tvarbhumate vibhumate prabhumate vājavate svāhetyāha | saṃvathsaro vai saviturbhumān vibhumānprabhumān vājavān | tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | yamāya tvā'ṃgirasvate pitṛmate svāhetyāha | prāṇo vai yamo'ṃgirasvānpitṛmān
5.7.d: अप्सु वै वरुण आदित्यवान् । तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । बृहस्पतये त्वा विश्वदेव्यावते स्वाहेत्याह । ब्रह्म वै देवानां बृहस्पतिः । ब्रह्मण एवैनं जुहोति । सवित्रे त्वर्भुमते विभुमते प्रभुमते वाजवते स्वाहेत्याह । संवथ्सरो वै सवितुर्भुमान् विभुमान्प्रभुमान् वाजवान् । तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । यमाय त्वाऽंगिरस्वते पितृमते स्वाहेत्याह । प्राणो वै यमोऽंगिरस्वान्पितृमान्
5.7.m:
Varuṇa in the waters is accompanied by the Ādityas; to him he offers it. He says, "To Bṛhaspati accompanied by the Viśvedevas, svāhā!" Bṛhaspati is the brahman among the gods; to the brahman he offers it. He says, "To Savitṛ accompanied by the Ṛbhus, the all-pervading, the mighty, rich in food, svāhā!" The year is Savitṛ accompanied by the Ṛbhus, the all-pervading, the mighty, rich in food; to it he offers it. He says, "To Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases, accompanied by the fathers, svāhā!" The vital breath is Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases and the fathers.

To him he offers it. He offers it to these very deities. They amount to ten; the virāj has ten syllables. The virāj is food; through the virāj he secures food. By means of the two Rauhiṇa [offerings] the gods went to the heavenly world. That is why the two Rauhiṇas are called Rauhiṇa. Because there are the two Rauhiṇas, the sacrificer goes to the heavenly world through the two Rauhiṇas. He says, "May day, the light, be pleased with the banner, the good light with light, svāhā! May night, the light, be pleased with the banner, the good light with light, svāhā!" He thereby supported Āditya in yonder world with day from above, with night from below. Therefore yonder Āditya is supported in that world by day and night. [Catchwords:] "names of humans, cattle, let him sit, to Indra he says, he halves, they kill, he takes, for non-injury, he says five, accompanied by the Ādityas, svāhā, he says, accompanied by the fathers," and four.

5.7.s: tasmā evainaṃ juhoti | etābhya evainaṃ devatābhyo juhoti | daśa saṃpadyante | daśākṣarā virāṭ | annaṃ virāṭ | virājaivānnādyamavarundhe | rauhiṇābhyāṃ vai devāssuvargaṃ lokamāyann | tadrauhiṇayo rauhiṇatvam | yadrauhiṇau bhavataḥ | rauhiṇābhyāmeva tadyajamānassuvargaṃ lokameti | aharjyotiḥ ketunā juṣatāṃ sujyotirjyotiṣāg svāhā rātrirjyotiḥ ketunā juṣatāṃ sujyotirjyotiṣāg svāhetyāha | ādityameva tadamuṣmiṃ lloke'hnā parastāddādhāra | rātriyā avastāt | tasmādasāvādityo'muṣmiṃ lloke'horātrābhyāṃ dhṛtaḥ
5.7.d: तस्मा एवैनं जुहोति । एताभ्य एवैनं देवताभ्यो जुहोति । दश संपद्यन्ते । दशाक्षरा विराट् । अन्नं विराट् । विराजैवान्नाद्यमवरुन्धे । रौहिणाभ्यां वै देवास्सुवर्गं लोकमायन्न् । तद्रौहिणयो रौहिणत्वम् । यद्रौहिणौ भवतः । रौहिणाभ्यामेव तद्यजमानस्सुवर्गं लोकमेति । अहर्ज्योतिः केतुना जुषतां सुज्योतिर्ज्योतिषाग् स्वाहा रात्रिर्ज्योतिः केतुना जुषतां सुज्योतिर्ज्योतिषाग् स्वाहेत्याह । आदित्यमेव तदमुष्मिं ल्लोकेऽह्ना परस्ताद्दाधार । रात्रिया अवस्तात् । तस्मादसावादित्योऽमुष्मिं ल्लोकेऽहोरात्राभ्यां धृतः

5.8.s: viśvā āśā dakṣiṇasadityāha | viśvāneva devānprīṇāti | atho duriṣṭyā evainaṃ pāti | viśvāndevānayāḍihetyāha | viśvāneva devānbhāgadheyena samardhayati | svāhākṛtasya gharmasya madhoḥ pibatamaśvinetyāha | aśvināveva bhāgadheyena samardhayati | svāhā'gnaye yajñiyāya śaṃ yajurbhirityāha | abhyevainaṃ ghārayati | atho havirevākaḥ
5.8.d: विश्वा आशा दक्षिणसदित्याह । विश्वानेव देवान्प्रीणाति । अथो दुरिष्ट्या एवैनं पाति । विश्वान्देवानयाडिहेत्याह । विश्वानेव देवान्भागधेयेन समर्धयति । स्वाहाकृतस्य घर्मस्य मधोः पिबतमश्विनेत्याह । अश्विनावेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति । स्वाहाऽग्नये यज्ञियाय शं यजुर्भिरित्याह । अभ्येवैनं घारयति । अथो हविरेवाकः
5.8.m: He says, "May all quarters sit to the south." He satisfies all the gods. Moreover, he protects him from bad sacrifice. He says, "He has sacrificed to all the gods here." He enriches all the gods with their portion. He says, "O Aśvins, drink the sweet gharma made with svāhā!" He enriches the Aśvins with their portion. He says, "Svāhā to Agni worthy of sacrifice, welfare with the yajus formulas!" He sprinkles it. Moreover, he makes it an oblation.

5.8.s: aśvinā gharmaṃ pātaṃ hārdivānamahardivābhirūtibhirityāha | aśvināveva bhāgadheyena samardhayati | anu vāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī maṃsātāmityāhānumatyai | svāhendrāya svāhendrāvaḍityāha | indrāya hi puro hūyate | āśrāvyāha gharmasya yajeti | vaṣaṭkṛte juhoti | rakṣasāmapahatyai | anuyajati svagākṛtyai | gharmamapātamaśvinetyāha
5.8.d: अश्विना घर्मं पातं हार्दिवानमहर्दिवाभिरूतिभिरित्याह । अश्विनावेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति । अनु वां द्यावापृथिवी मंसातामित्याहानुमत्यै । स्वाहेन्द्राय स्वाहेन्द्रावडित्याह । इन्द्राय हि पुरो हूयते । आश्राव्याह घर्मस्य यजेति । वषट्कृते जुहोति । रक्षसामपहत्यै । अनुयजति स्वगाकृत्यै । घर्ममपातमश्विनेत्याह
5.8.m: He says, "O Aśvins, drink the gharma, the gladdener of the heart, day by day with aids!" He enriches the Aśvins with their portion. He says, "May sky and earth approve of you two," for the sake of assent. He says, "Svāhā to Indra, svāhā to Indra, vaṭ!" For it is offered in the east to Indra. Having called for the recitation, he says, "Recite for the offering of the gharma." He offers when the vaṣaṭ-call is made, to ward off the rakṣases. He performs the after-offering to make it acceptable. He says, "O Aśvins, you have drunk the gharma."

5.8.s: pūrvamevoditam | uttareṇābhigṛṇāti | anu vāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī amaṃsātāmityāhānumatyai | taṃ prāvyaṃ yathāvaṇṇamo dive namaḥ pṛthivyā ityāha | yathā yajurevaitat | divi dhā imaṃ yajñaṃ yajñamimaṃ divi dhā ityāha | suvargamevainaṃ lokaṃ gamayati | divaṃ gacchāntarikṣaṃ gaccha pṛthivīṃ gacchetyāha | eṣvevainaṃ lokeṣu pratiṣṭhāpayati | pañca pradiśo gacchetyāha
5.8.d: पूर्वमेवोदितम् । उत्तरेणाभिगृणाति । अनु वां द्यावापृथिवी अमंसातामित्याहानुमत्यै । तं प्राव्यं यथावण्णमो दिवे नमः पृथिव्या इत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । दिवि धा इमं यज्ञं यज्ञमिमं दिवि धा इत्याह । सुवर्गमेवैनं लोकं गमयति । दिवं गच्छान्तरिक्षं गच्छ पृथिवीं गच्छेत्याह । एष्वेवैनं लोकेषु प्रतिष्ठापयति । पञ्च प्रदिशो गच्छेत्याह
5.8.m: What was uttered earlier, he addresses with the later [formula]. He says, "Sky and earth have approved of you two," for the sake of assent. He says, "That worthy of protection, as is proper, homage to the sky, homage to the earth!" This is just according to the yajus. He says, "Place this sacrifice in the sky, place this sacrifice in the sky!" He makes him go to the heavenly world. He says, "Go to the sky, go to the intermediate space, go to the earth!" He establishes him in these worlds. He says, "Go to the five directions!"

5.8.s: dikṣvevainaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati | devāngharmapāngaccha pitṝngharmapāngacchetyāha | ubhayeṣvevainaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati | yatpinvate | varṣukaḥ parjanyo bhavati | tasmātpinvamānaḥ puṇyaḥ | yatprāṅpinvate | taddevānām | yaddakṣiṇā | tatpitṛṇām
5.8.d: दिक्ष्वेवैनं प्रतिष्ठापयति । देवान्घर्मपान्गच्छ पितॄन्घर्मपान्गच्छेत्याह । उभयेष्वेवैनं प्रतिष्ठापयति । यत्पिन्वते । वर्षुकः पर्जन्यो भवति । तस्मात्पिन्वमानः पुण्यः । यत्प्राङ्पिन्वते । तद्देवानाम् । यद्दक्षिणा । तत्पितृणाम्
5.8.m: He establishes him in the directions. He says, "Go to the gods who drink the gharma, go to the fathers who drink the gharma!" He establishes him in both. When it overflows, Parjanya becomes rainy; therefore, overflowing is auspicious. When it overflows toward the east, that belongs to the gods; when to the south, that belongs to the fathers.

5.8.s: yatpratyak | tanmanuṣyāṇām | yadudaṅṅ | tadrudrāṇām | prāñcamudañcaṃ pinvayati | devatrā'kaḥ | atho khalu | sarvā anu diśaḥ pinvayati | sarvā diśassamedhante | antaḥparidhi pinvayati
5.8.d: यत्प्रत्यक् । तन्मनुष्याणाम् । यदुदङ्ङ् । तद्रुद्राणाम् । प्राञ्चमुदञ्चं पिन्वयति । देवत्राऽकः । अथो खलु । सर्वा अनु दिशः पिन्वयति । सर्वा दिशस्समेधन्ते । अन्तःपरिधि पिन्वयति
5.8.m: When toward the west, that belongs to humans; when toward the north, that belongs to the Rudras. He causes it to overflow toward the northeast; he has placed it among the gods. Moreover, he causes it to overflow along all the directions; all the directions prosper. He causes it to overflow within the enclosing sticks.

5.8.s: tejaso'skandāya | iṣe pīpihyūrje pīpihītyāha | iṣamevorjaṃ yajamāne dadhāti | yajamānāya pīpihītyāha | yajamānāyaivaitāmāśiṣamāśāste | mahyaṃ jyaiṣṭhyāya pīpihītyāha | ātmana evaitāmāśiṣamāśāste | tviṣyai tvā dyumnāya tvendriyāya tvā bhūtyai tvetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | dharmā'si sudharmā me nyasme brahmāṇi dhārayetyāha
5.8.d: तेजसोऽस्कन्दाय । इषे पीपिह्यूर्जे पीपिहीत्याह । इषमेवोर्जं यजमाने दधाति । यजमानाय पीपिहीत्याह । यजमानायैवैतामाशिषमाशास्ते । मह्यं ज्यैष्ठ्याय पीपिहीत्याह । आत्मन एवैतामाशिषमाशास्ते । त्विष्यै त्वा द्युम्नाय त्वेन्द्रियाय त्वा भूत्यै त्वेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । धर्माऽसि सुधर्मा मे न्यस्मे ब्रह्माणि धारयेत्याह
5.8.m: [He makes it swell] within the enclosing sticks, so that his brilliance does not spill. He says: 'Swell for food! Swell for strength!' He establishes food and strength in the sacrificer. He says: 'Swell for the sacrificer!' It is for the sacrificer that he pronounces this blessing. He says: 'Swell for me, for supremacy!' It is for himself that he pronounces this blessing. He says: 'Thee for splendor, thee for radiance, thee for faculty, thee for prosperity!' This is just according to the yajus. He says: 'Thou art the upholder, good upholder, hold fast the brahmans among us!'

5.8.s: brahmannevainaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati | nettvā vātasskandayāditi yadyabhicaret | amuṣya tvā prāṇe sādayāmyamunā saha nirarthaṃ gaccheti brūyādyaṃ dviṣyāt | yameva dveṣṭi | tenainaṃ saha nirarthaṃ gamayati | pūṣṇe śarase svāhetyāha | yā eva devatā hutabhāgāḥ | tābhya evainaṃ juhoti | grāvabhyassvāhetyāha | yā evāntarikṣe vācaḥ
5.8.d: ब्रह्मन्नेवैनं प्रतिष्ठापयति । नेत्त्वा वातस्स्कन्दयादिति यद्यभिचरेत् । अमुष्य त्वा प्राणे सादयाम्यमुना सह निरर्थं गच्छेति ब्रूयाद्यं द्विष्यात् । यमेव द्वेष्टि । तेनैनं सह निरर्थं गमयति । पूष्णे शरसे स्वाहेत्याह । या एव देवता हुतभागाः । ताभ्य एवैनं जुहोति । ग्रावभ्यस्स्वाहेत्याह । या एवान्तरिक्षे वाचः
5.8.m:
He firmly establishes it in brahman. If he should perform sorcery [with the thought], 'Lest the wind spill thee,' he should say concerning him whom he hates: 'I set thee down in the breath of so-and-so; go to destruction along with so-and-so!' Whomever he hates, him he sends to destruction along with it. He says: 'To Pūṣan the strong, svāhā!' Whatever deities have a share in the offering, to them he offers it. He says: 'To the pressing-stones, svāhā!' Whatever voices are in the intermediate space,

to them he offers it. He says: 'To the Pratiras, svāhā!' The gods, the Pratiras, are indeed the breaths; to them he offers it. He says: 'To Heaven and Earth, svāhā!' To Heaven and Earth he offers it. He says: 'To the fathers who drink the gharma, svāhā!' Those who have sacrificed are indeed the fathers who drink the gharma; to them he offers it.

5.8.s: tābhya evainaṃ juhoti | pratirebhyaḥ svāhetyāha | prāṇā vai devāḥ pratirāḥ | tebhya evainaṃ juhoti | dyāvāpṛthivībhyāg svāhetyāha | dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmevainaṃ juhoti | pitṛbhyo gharmapebhyaḥ svāhetyāha | ye vai yajvānaḥ | te pitaro gharmapāḥ | tebhya evainaṃ juhoti
5.8.d: ताभ्य एवैनं जुहोति । प्रतिरेभ्यः स्वाहेत्याह । प्राणा वै देवाः प्रतिराः । तेभ्य एवैनं जुहोति । द्यावापृथिवीभ्याग् स्वाहेत्याह । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामेवैनं जुहोति । पितृभ्यो घर्मपेभ्यः स्वाहेत्याह । ये वै यज्वानः । ते पितरो घर्मपाः । तेभ्य एवैनं जुहोति

5.8.s: rudrāya rudrahotre svāhetyāha | rudrameva bhāgadheyena samardhayati | sarvatassamanakti | sarvata eva rudraṃ niravadayate | udañcaṃ nirasyati | eṣā vai rudrasya dik | svāyāmeva diśi rudraṃ niravadayate | apa upaspṛśati medhyatvāya | nānvīkṣeta | yadanvīkṣeta
5.8.d: रुद्राय रुद्रहोत्रे स्वाहेत्याह । रुद्रमेव भागधेयेन समर्धयति । सर्वतस्समनक्ति । सर्वत एव रुद्रं निरवदयते । उदञ्चं निरस्यति । एषा वै रुद्रस्य दिक् । स्वायामेव दिशि रुद्रं निरवदयते । अप उपस्पृशति मेध्यत्वाय । नान्वीक्षेत । यदन्वीक्षेत
5.8.m: He says: 'To Rudra, the Rudra-hotṛ, svāhā!' He provides Rudra with his share. He anoints [the vessel] all around; he appeases Rudra on all sides. He throws it out towards the north. That is indeed the direction of Rudra; he appeases Rudra in his own direction. He touches water for purification. He should not look after it. If he were to look after it,

5.8.s: cakṣurasya pramāyukaṃ syāt | tasmānnānvīkṣyaḥ | apīparo mā'hno rātriyai mā pāhyeṣā te agne samittayā samidhyasvāyurme dā varcasā mā'ṃjīrityāha | āyurevāsminvarco dadhāti | apīparo mā rātriyā ahno mā pāhyeṣā te agne samittayā samidhyasvāyurme dā varcasā mā'ṃjīrityāha | āyurevāsminvarco dadhāti | agnirjyotirjyotiragniḥ svāhā sūryo jyotirjyotissūryaḥ svāhetyāha | yathā yajurevaitat | brahmavādino vadanti | hotavyamagnihotrām na hotavyāmiti
5.8.d: चक्षुरस्य प्रमायुकं स्यात् । तस्मान्नान्वीक्ष्यः । अपीपरो माऽह्नो रात्रियै मा पाह्येषा ते अग्ने समित्तया समिध्यस्वायुर्मे दा वर्चसा माऽंजीरित्याह । आयुरेवास्मिन्वर्चो दधाति । अपीपरो मा रात्रिया अह्नो मा पाह्येषा ते अग्ने समित्तया समिध्यस्वायुर्मे दा वर्चसा माऽंजीरित्याह । आयुरेवास्मिन्वर्चो दधाति । अग्निर्ज्योतिर्ज्योतिरग्निः स्वाहा सूर्यो ज्योतिर्ज्योतिस्सूर्यः स्वाहेत्याह । यथा यजुरेवैतत् । ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति । होतव्यमग्निहोत्राम् न होतव्यामिति
5.8.m: his sight would perish. Therefore, he should not look after it. He says: 'Thou hast carried me across the day; protect me from the night! This is thy kindling-stick, O Agni; kindle thyself with it; grant me lifespan; anoint me with radiance!' He places lifespan and radiance in him. He says: 'Thou hast carried me across the night; protect me from the day! This is thy kindling-stick, O Agni; kindle thyself with it; grant me lifespan; anoint me with radiance!' He places lifespan and radiance in him. He says: 'Agni is light, light is Agni, svāhā! Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā!' This is just according to the yajus. The knowers of brahman discuss: 'Is the Agnihotra to be offered, or is it not to be offered?'

5.8.s: yadyajuṣā juhuyāt | ayathāpūrvamāhutī juhuyāt | yanna juhuyāt | agniḥ parābhavet | bhūssvāhetyeva hotavyam | yathāpūrvamāhutī juhoti | nāgniḥ parābhavati | hutaṃ havirmadhu havirityāha | svadayatyevainam | indratame'gnāvityāha
5.8.d: यद्यजुषा जुहुयात् । अयथापूर्वमाहुती जुहुयात् । यन्न जुहुयात् । अग्निः पराभवेत् । भूस्स्वाहेत्येव होतव्यम् । यथापूर्वमाहुती जुहोति । नाग्निः पराभवति । हुतं हविर्मधु हविरित्याह । स्वदयत्येवैनम् । इन्द्रतमेऽग्नावित्याह
5.8.m: If he were to offer with a yajus, he would offer the oblations out of proper sequence. If he were not to offer, Agni would perish. He should offer with just 'Bhūḥ, svāhā!' He offers the oblations in proper sequence; Agni does not perish. He says: 'The oblation is offered, the oblation is honey.' He sweetens it. He says: 'In Agni, most like Indra.'

5.8.s: prāṇo vā indratamo'gniḥ | prāṇa evainamindratame'gnau juhoti | pitā no'si mā mā hiṃsīrityāhāhiṃsāyai | aśyāma te deva gharma madhumato vājavataḥ pitumata ityāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | svadhāvino'śīmahi tvā mā mā hiṃsīrityāhāhiṃsāyai | tejasā vā ete vyṛdhyante | ye pravargyeṇa caranti | prāśñanti | teja evātmandadhate
5.8.d: प्राणो वा इन्द्रतमोऽग्निः । प्राण एवैनमिन्द्रतमेऽग्नौ जुहोति । पिता नोऽसि मा मा हिंसीरित्याहाहिंसायै । अश्याम ते देव घर्म मधुमतो वाजवतः पितुमत इत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । स्वधाविनोऽशीमहि त्वा मा मा हिंसीरित्याहाहिंसायै । तेजसा वा एते व्यृध्यन्ते । ये प्रवर्ग्येण चरन्ति । प्राश्ञन्ति । तेज एवात्मन्दधते
5.8.m: Vital breath is indeed Agni, most like Indra; he offers it in vital breath, in Agni, most like Indra. He says: 'Thou art our father, harm me not!' for harmlessness. He says: 'May we eat of thee, O divine gharma, full of honey, rich in sustenance, rich in nourishment.' It is this blessing that he invokes. He says: 'Possessing self-power, may we partake of thee; harm me not!' for harmlessness. They who perform the pravargya are deprived of brilliance. They consume [it]; they place brilliance in themselves.

5.8.s: saṃvathsaraṃ na māṃsamaśñīyāt | na rāmāmupeyāt | na mṛnmayena pibet | nāsya rāma ucchiṣṭaṃ pibet | teja eva tathsaṃśyati | devāsurāssaṃyattā āsann | te devā vijayamupayantaḥ | vibhrāji saurye brahma saṃnyadadhata | yatkiṃca divākīrtyam | tadetenaiva vratenāgopāyat | tasmādetadvrataṃ cāryam | tejaso gopīthāya | tasmādetāni yajūṃṣi vibhrājaḥ sauryasyetyāhuḥ | svāhā tvā sūryasya raśmibhya iti prātassaṃ sādayati | svāhā tvā nakṣatrebhya iti sāyam | etā vā etasya devatāḥ | tābhirevainaṃ samardhayati
5.8.d: संवथ्सरं न मांसमश्ञीयात् । न रामामुपेयात् । न मृन्मयेन पिबेत् । नास्य राम उच्छिष्टं पिबेत् । तेज एव तथ्संश्यति । देवासुरास्संयत्ता आसन्न् । ते देवा विजयमुपयन्तः । विभ्राजि सौर्ये ब्रह्म संन्यदधत । यत्किंच दिवाकीर्त्यम् । तदेतेनैव व्रतेनागोपायत् । तस्मादेतद्व्रतं चार्यम् । तेजसो गोपीथाय । तस्मादेतानि यजूंषि विभ्राजः सौर्यस्येत्याहुः । स्वाहा त्वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिभ्य इति प्रातस्सं सादयति । स्वाहा त्वा नक्षत्रेभ्य इति सायम् । एता वा एतस्य देवताः । ताभिरेवैनं समर्धयति
5.8.m: For a year he should not eat meat, he should not approach a low-caste woman, he should not drink from an earthen vessel, nor should a low-caste person drink his leftovers. Thus he sharpens brilliance. The gods and the asuras were in conflict. The gods, striving for victory, deposited their sacred lore in the gleaming solar power, along with whatever was to be chanted by day. By this observance they protected it. Therefore this observance is to be kept, to guard brilliance. Therefore they say that these yajuses belong to the gleaming solar power. In the morning he places it with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the rays of the sun!' In the evening with: 'Svāhā to thee, to the constellations!' These are indeed its deities; with them he enriches it. 'The Aśvins did,' he said; 'Go to the quarters,' he said; 'of the fathers'; he makes it swell within the enclosing sticks; 'Hold,' he said; 'voices'; 'drinkers of gharma, to them he offers it'; 'he should look after'; 'Is it to be offered?'; 'in Agni,' he said; 'they place; he protected', and seven.

5.9.s: gharma yā te divi śugiti tisra āhutīrjuhoti | chandobhirevāsyaibhyo lokebhyaḥ śucamavayajate | iyatyagre juhoti | atheyatyatheyati | traya ime lokāḥ | ebhya eva lokebhyaḥ śucamavayajate | anu no'dyānumatirityāhānumatyai | divastvā paraspāyā ityāha | diva evemān lokāndādhāra | brahmaṇastvā paraspāyā ityāha
5.9.d: घर्म या ते दिवि शुगिति तिस्र आहुतीर्जुहोति । छन्दोभिरेवास्यैभ्यो लोकेभ्यः शुचमवयजते । इयत्यग्रे जुहोति । अथेयत्यथेयति । त्रय इमे लोकाः । एभ्य एव लोकेभ्यः शुचमवयजते । अनु नोऽद्यानुमतिरित्याहानुमत्यै । दिवस्त्वा परस्पाया इत्याह । दिव एवेमान् लोकान्दाधार । ब्रह्मणस्त्वा परस्पाया इत्याह
5.9.m: With 'O gharma, what grief of thine is in the sky,' he offers three oblations. By means of the meters, he removes grief from these worlds for him. First he offers [a stick] of such size, then of such size, then of such size. These worlds are three; he removes grief from these worlds. With 'May Anumati favor us today,' he offers for Anumati's favor. He says: 'Thee for the distant protection of heaven.' From heaven he upholds these worlds. He says: 'Thee for the distant protection of brahman.'

5.9.s: eṣveva lokeṣu prajā dādhāra | prāṇasya tvā paraspāyā ityāha | prajāsveva prāṇāndādhāra | śiro vā etadyajñasya | yatpravargyaḥ | asau khalu vā ādityaḥ pravargyaḥ | taṃ yaddakṣiṇā pratyañcamudañcamudvāsayet | jihmaṃ yajñasya śiro haret | prāñcamudvāsayati | purastādeva yajñasya śiraḥ pratidadhāti
5.9.d: एष्वेव लोकेषु प्रजा दाधार । प्राणस्य त्वा परस्पाया इत्याह । प्रजास्वेव प्राणान्दाधार । शिरो वा एतद्यज्ञस्य । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । असौ खलु वा आदित्यः प्रवर्ग्यः । तं यद्दक्षिणा प्रत्यञ्चमुदञ्चमुद्वासयेत् । जिह्मं यज्ञस्य शिरो हरेत् । प्राञ्चमुद्वासयति । पुरस्तादेव यज्ञस्य शिरः प्रतिदधाति
5.9.m:
In these worlds he upholds creatures. He says: 'Thee for the distant protection of breath.' In creatures he upholds the vital breaths. The head of the sacrifice is indeed this: the pravargya. Yonder Āditya is indeed the pravargya. If he were to remove it to the south, to the west, or to the north, he would lead the head of the sacrifice awry. He removes it to the east; in front he replaces the head of the sacrifice.

He removes it to the east; therefore yonder Āditya rises in the east. They carry along the tongs, the supporting implements, the fans, and the fire-stirrers. He makes it possessed of its self, possessed of its body. Possessed of his self does he become in yonder world, who knows this. They are made of udumbara wood. Udumbara is vigor; he obtains vigor. Following along the path,

5.9.s: prāñcamudvāsayati | tasmādasāvādityaḥ purastādudeti | śaphopayamāndhavitrāṇi dhṛṣṭī ityanvavaharanti | sātmānamevainaṃ satanuṃ karoti | sātmā'muṣmiṃ lloke bhavati | ya evaṃ veda | audumbarāṇi bhavanti | ūrgvā udumbaraḥ | ūrjamevāvarundhe | vartmanā vā anvitya
5.9.d: प्राञ्चमुद्वासयति । तस्मादसावादित्यः पुरस्तादुदेति । शफोपयमान्धवित्राणि धृष्टी इत्यन्ववहरन्ति । सात्मानमेवैनं सतनुं करोति । सात्माऽमुष्मिं ल्लोके भवति । य एवं वेद । औदुम्बराणि भवन्ति । ऊर्ग्वा उदुम्बरः । ऊर्जमेवावरुन्धे । वर्त्मना वा अन्वित्य

5.9.s: yajñaṃ rakṣāṃsi jighāṃsanti | sāmnā prastotā'nvavaiti | sāma vai rakṣohā | rakṣasāmapahatyai | trirnidhanamupaiti | traya ime lokāḥ | ebhya eva lokebhyo rakṣāṃsyapahanti | puruṣaḥ puruṣo nidhanamupaiti | puruṣaḥ puruṣo hi rakṣasvī | rakṣasāmapahatyai
5.9.d: यज्ञं रक्षांसि जिघांसन्ति । साम्ना प्रस्तोताऽन्ववैति । साम वै रक्षोहा । रक्षसामपहत्यै । त्रिर्निधनमुपैति । त्रय इमे लोकाः । एभ्य एव लोकेभ्यो रक्षांस्यपहन्ति । पुरुषः पुरुषो निधनमुपैति । पुरुषः पुरुषो हि रक्षस्वी । रक्षसामपहत्यै
5.9.m: the rakṣases seek to destroy the sacrifice. The Prastotṛ accompanies it with a sāman. The sāman is indeed a slayer of rakṣases, for the destruction of the rakṣases. He performs the finale three times. These worlds are three; he destroys the rakṣases from these worlds. Man by man, he performs the finale, for man by man is possessed by rakṣases, for the destruction of the rakṣases.

5.9.s: yatpṛthivyāmudvāsayet | pṛthivīṃ śucā'rpayet | yadapsu | apaḥ śucā'rpayet | yadoṣadhīṣu | oṣadhīḥ śucā'rpayet | yadvanaspatiṣu | vanaspatīñchucā'rpayet | hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyodvāsayati | amṛtaṃ vai hiraṇyam
5.9.d: यत्पृथिव्यामुद्वासयेत् । पृथिवीं शुचाऽर्पयेत् । यदप्सु । अपः शुचाऽर्पयेत् । यदोषधीषु । ओषधीः शुचाऽर्पयेत् । यद्वनस्पतिषु । वनस्पतीञ्छुचाऽर्पयेत् । हिरण्यं निधायोद्वासयति । अमृतं वै हिरण्यम्
5.9.m: If he were to remove it on the earth, he would afflict the earth with heat. If in the waters, he would afflict the waters with heat. If among plants, he would afflict plants with heat. If among trees, he would afflict trees with heat. Having laid down gold, he removes it. Gold is indeed immortal life;

5.9.s: amṛta evainaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati | valgurasi śaṃyudhāyā iti triḥ pariṣiñcanparyeti | trivṛdvā agniḥ | yāvānevāgniḥ | tasya śucaṃ śamayati | triḥ punaḥ paryeti | ṣaṭtha saṃpadyante | ṣaḍvā ṛtavaḥ | ṛtubhirevāsya śucaṃ śamayati | catussraktirnābhirṛtasyetyāha
5.9.d: अमृत एवैनं प्रतिष्ठापयति । वल्गुरसि शंयुधाया इति त्रिः परिषिञ्चन्पर्येति । त्रिवृद्वा अग्निः । यावानेवाग्निः । तस्य शुचं शमयति । त्रिः पुनः पर्येति । षट्थ संपद्यन्ते । षड्वा ऋतवः । ऋतुभिरेवास्य शुचं शमयति । चतुस्स्रक्तिर्नाभिरृतस्येत्याह
5.9.m: he establishes it in immortal life. Saying 'Thou art attractive, bestower of peace,' he goes around sprinkling it three times. Agni is threefold; as great as Agni is, so he appeases his heat. He goes around three times more; they amount to six. There are six seasons; by the seasons he appeases his heat. He says: 'Four-cornered, the navel of cosmic order.'

5.9.s: iyaṃ vā ṛtam | tasyā eṣa eva nābhiḥ | yatpravargyaḥ | tasmādevamāha | sado viśvāyurityāha | sado hīyam | apa dveṣo apa hvara ityāha bhrātṛvyāpanutyai | gharmaitatte'nnametatpurīṣamiti dadhnā madhumiśreṇa pūrayati | ūrgvā annādyaṃ dadhi | ūrjaivainamannādyena samardhayati
5.9.d: इयं वा ऋतम् । तस्या एष एव नाभिः । यत्प्रवर्ग्यः । तस्मादेवमाह । सदो विश्वायुरित्याह । सदो हीयम् । अप द्वेषो अप ह्वर इत्याह भ्रातृव्यापनुत्यै । घर्मैतत्तेऽन्नमेतत्पुरीषमिति दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण पूरयति । ऊर्ग्वा अन्नाद्यं दधि । ऊर्जैवैनमन्नाद्येन समर्धयति
5.9.m: This [earth] is indeed truth. This very one is its navel, namely the pravargya. Therefore he speaks thus. "Seat of all life," he says, for this [earth] is a seat. "Away with hatred, away with malice!" he says, for the driving away of rivals. "O gharma, this is your food, this your rubbish," thus he fills [it] with curd mixed with honey. Curd is vigor, the eating of food; with vigor and with the eating of food he prospers him.

5.9.s: anaśanāyuko bhavati | ya evaṃ veda | rantirnāmāsi divyo gandharva ityāha | rūpamevāsyaitanmahimānaṃ rantiṃ bandhutāṃ vyācaṣṭe | samahamāyuṣā saṃ prāṇenetyāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | vyasau yo'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma ityāha | abhicāra evāsyaiṣaḥ | acikradadvṛṣā harirityāha | vṛṣā hyeṣaḥ
5.9.d: अनशनायुको भवति । य एवं वेद । रन्तिर्नामासि दिव्यो गन्धर्व इत्याह । रूपमेवास्यैतन्महिमानं रन्तिं बन्धुतां व्याचष्टे । समहमायुषा सं प्राणेनेत्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । व्यसौ योऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इत्याह । अभिचार एवास्यैषः । अचिक्रदद्वृषा हरिरित्याह । वृषा ह्येषः
5.9.m: He does not become hungry who knows thus. "Delight by name are you, the heavenly gandharva," he says; thus he declares his form, his greatness, his delight, his kinship. "May I be united with lifespan, united with vital breath," he says; this very blessing he invokes. "Broken be that one who hates us and whom we hate!" he says; this is indeed his act of sorcery. "The virile bull, the tawny one, has roared," he says, for he is a bull,

5.9.s: vṛṣā hariḥ | mahānmitro na darśata ityāha | stautyevainametat | cidasi samudrayonirityāha | svāmevainaṃ yoniṃ gamayati | namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīrityāhāhiṃsāyai | viśvāvasuṃ somagandharvamityāha | yadevāsya kriyamāṇasyāntaryanti | tadevāsyaitenāpyāyayati | viśvāvasurabhi tanno gṛṇātvityāha
5.9.d: वृषा हरिः । महान्मित्रो न दर्शत इत्याह । स्तौत्येवैनमेतत् । चिदसि समुद्रयोनिरित्याह । स्वामेवैनं योनिं गमयति । नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरित्याहाहिंसायै । विश्वावसुं सोमगन्धर्वमित्याह । यदेवास्य क्रियमाणस्यान्तर्यन्ति । तदेवास्यैतेनाप्याययति । विश्वावसुरभि तन्नो गृणात्वित्याह
5.9.m: a virile bull, tawny. "Great, lovely like Mitra," he says; thereby he indeed praises him. "You are thought, having the ocean as your womb," he says; he causes him to go to his own womb. "Homage be to you; do not harm me!" he says, for the sake of non-harm. "Viśvāvasu, the Soma-gandharva," he says; whatever of him as he is being made they interrupt, that very [part] he swells for him with this. "May Viśvāvasu proclaim that for us," he says;

5.9.s: pūrvamevoditam | uttareṇābhigṛṇāti | dhiyo hinvāno dhiya inno avyādityāha | ṛtūnevāsmai kalpayati | prāsāṃ gandharvo amṛtāni vocadityāha | prāṇā vā amṛtāḥ | prāṇānevāsmai kalpayati | etattvaṃ deva gharma devo devānupāgā ityāha | devo hyeṣa sandevānupaiti | idamahaṃ manuṣyo manuṣyānityāha
5.9.d: पूर्वमेवोदितम् । उत्तरेणाभिगृणाति । धियो हिन्वानो धिय इन्नो अव्यादित्याह । ऋतूनेवास्मै कल्पयति । प्रासां गन्धर्वो अमृतानि वोचदित्याह । प्राणा वा अमृताः । प्राणानेवास्मै कल्पयति । एतत्त्वं देव घर्म देवो देवानुपागा इत्याह । देवो ह्येष सन्देवानुपैति । इदमहं मनुष्यो मनुष्यानित्याह
5.9.m: what was spoken before, he confirms with what follows. "Urging our thoughts, may he protect our thoughts," he says; he arranges the seasons for him. "May the gandharva speak of their immortal [realms]," he says; the vital breaths are indeed immortal; he arranges the vital breaths for him. "Being a god, you have gone, O god gharma, to the gods," he says, for being a god, he goes to the gods. "Here I, a mortal, to mortals," he says;

5.9.s: manuṣyo hi | eṣa sanmanuṣyānupaiti | īśvaro vai pravargyamudvāsayann | prajāṃ paśūnthsomapīthamanūdvāsaḥ somapīthānumehi | saha prajayā saha rāyaspoṣeṇetyāha | prajāmeva paśūnthsomapīthamātmandhatte | sumitrā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santvityāha | āśiṣamevaitāmāśāste | durmitrāstasmai bhūyāsuryo'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣma ityāha | abhicāra evāsyaiṣaḥ | pra vā eṣo'smāllokāccyavate | yaḥ pravargyamudvāsayati | udu tyaṃ citramiti saurībhyāmṛgbhyāṃ punaretya gārhapatye juhoti | ayaṃ vai loko gārhapatyaḥ | asminneva loke pratitiṣṭhati | asau khalu vā ādityassuvargo lokaḥ | yathsaurī bhavataḥ | tenaiva suvargāllokānnaiti
5.9.d: मनुष्यो हि । एष सन्मनुष्यानुपैति । ईश्वरो वै प्रवर्ग्यमुद्वासयन्न् । प्रजां पशून्थ्सोमपीथमनूद्वासः सोमपीथानुमेहि । सह प्रजया सह रायस्पोषेणेत्याह । प्रजामेव पशून्थ्सोमपीथमात्मन्धत्ते । सुमित्रा न आप ओषधयः सन्त्वित्याह । आशिषमेवैतामाशास्ते । दुर्मित्रास्तस्मै भूयासुर्योऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्म इत्याह । अभिचार एवास्यैषः । प्र वा एषोऽस्माल्लोकाच्च्यवते । यः प्रवर्ग्यमुद्वासयति । उदु त्यं चित्रमिति सौरीभ्यामृग्भ्यां पुनरेत्य गार्हपत्ये जुहोति । अयं वै लोको गार्हपत्यः । अस्मिन्नेव लोके प्रतितिष्ठति । असौ खलु वा आदित्यस्सुवर्गो लोकः । यथ्सौरी भवतः । तेनैव सुवर्गाल्लोकान्नैति
5.9.m: for he, being a mortal, goes to mortals. Being capable of it, when removing the pravargya, "Following after the offspring, the cattle, the drinking of Soma, remove yourself; come after the drinking of Soma with offspring, with increase of wealth," he says; he places offspring, cattle, and the drinking of Soma in himself. "May waters and plants be friendly to us," he says; this very blessing he invokes. "May they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate," he says; this is his act of sorcery. He departs from this world who removes the pravargya. Returning, he offers in the gārhapatya with two verses to Sūrya, beginning with "Up that wondrous [banner of the gods]" and "[The wondrous face of the gods has arisen]"; this world is the gārhapatya; he is established in this very world. That Āditya indeed is the heaven-world; because there are two [verses] to Sūrya, he does not depart from the heaven-world. "From brahman, your protector from afar," he says; he places; following; with rakṣas, for the slaying of rakṣas; gold; he says; for he causes to prosper; "may he proclaim," he says; "to mortals," he says; his this; and eight.

5.10.s: prajāpatiṃ vai devāḥ śukraṃ payo'duhrann | tadebhyo na vyabhavat | tadagnirvyakarot | tāni śukriyāṇi sāmānyabhavann | teṣāṃ yo raso'tyakṣarat | tāni śukrayajūgṣyabhavan | śukriyāṇāṃ vā etāni śukriyāṇi | sāmapayasaṃ vā etayoranyat | devānāmanyatpayaḥ | yadgoḥ payaḥ
