7.7.m: Earth, intermediate space, sky, the quarters, the intermediate quarters; Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the moon, the constellations; the waters, the plants, the trees, space, the body: this is with respect to the elements. Now with respect to the self: the outgoing breath, the diffused breath, the downward breath, the upward breath, the equalising breath; sight, hearing, mind, speech, skin; hide, flesh, sinew, bone, marrow. Having distinguished this, the seer said: 'Fivefold, indeed, is all this; by the fivefold does one support the fivefold.' / [Pratīka index: sarvam, and one.]

7.8.s: omiti brahma | omitīdaṃ sarvam | omityetadanukṛti ha sma vā apyo śrāvayetyāśrāvayanti | omiti sāmāni gāyanti | oṃ śomiti śastrāṇi śaṃsanti | omityadhvaryuḥ pratigaraṃ pratigṛṇāti | omiti brahmā prasauti | omityagnihotramanujānāti | omiti brāhmaṇaḥ pravakṣyannāha brahmopāpnavānīti | brahmaivopāpnoti
7.8.d: ओमिति ब्रह्म । ओमितीदं सर्वम् । ओमित्येतदनुकृति ह स्म वा अप्यो श्रावयेत्याश्रावयन्ति । ओमिति सामानि गायन्ति । ओं शोमिति शस्त्राणि शंसन्ति । ओमित्यध्वर्युः प्रतिगरं प्रतिगृणाति । ओमिति ब्रह्मा प्रसौति । ओमित्यग्निहोत्रमनुजानाति । ओमिति ब्राह्मणः प्रवक्ष्यन्नाह ब्रह्मोपाप्नवानीति । ब्रह्मैवोपाप्नोति
7.8.m: Om is brahman. Om is all this. Om is that assent; for indeed they recite, 'Make [them] listen!' with Om. With Om they sing the sāmans. With 'Oṃ śom' they recite the praise-hymns. With Om the Adhvaryu pronounces the response. With Om the Brahmā priest gives his assent. With Om one permits the Agnihotra. With Om a brāhmaṇa, about to recite, says, 'May I attain brahman!' He attains brahman indeed. / [Pratīka index: om, ten.]

7.9.s: ṛtaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca | satyaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca | tapaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | damaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | śamaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | agnayaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | agnihotraṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca | atithayaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | mānuṣaṃ ca svādhyāyapravacane ca | prajā ca svādhyāyapravacane ca | prajanaśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | prajātiśca svādhyāyapravacane ca | satyamiti satyavacā rāthītaraḥ | tapa iti taponityaḥ pauruśiṣṭiḥ | svādhyāyapravacane eveti nāko maudgalyaḥ | taddhi tapastaddhi tapaḥ
7.9.d: ऋतं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । सत्यं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । तपश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । दमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । शमश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अग्नयश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अग्निहोत्रं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । अतिथयश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । मानुषं च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजा च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजनश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । प्रजातिश्च स्वाध्यायप्रवचने च । सत्यमिति सत्यवचा राथीतरः । तप इति तपोनित्यः पौरुशिष्टिः । स्वाध्यायप्रवचने एवेति नाको मौद्गल्यः । तद्धि तपस्तद्धि तपः
7.9.m: Right order, and study and teaching. Truth, and study and teaching. Ascetic heat, and study and teaching. Self-control, and study and teaching. Quietude, and study and teaching. The sacred fires, and study and teaching. The Agnihotra, and study and teaching. Guests, and study and teaching. What is human, and study and teaching. Progeny, and study and teaching. Procreation, and study and teaching. Propagation, and study and teaching. 'Truth,' says Satyavacas Rāthītara. 'Ascetic heat,' says Taponitya Pauruśiṣṭi. 'Study and teaching alone,' says Nāka Maudgalya; for that is ascetic heat, that is ascetic heat. / [Pratīka index: prajā ca svādhyāyapravacane ca, and six.]

7.10.s: ahaṃ vṛkṣasya rerivā | kīrtiḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ gireriva | ūrdhvapavitro vājinīva svamṛtamasmi | draviṇaṃ savarcasam | sumedhā amṛtokṣitaḥ | iti triśaṅkorvedānuvacanam
7.10.d: अहं वृक्षस्य रेरिवा । कीर्तिः पृष्ठं गिरेरिव । ऊर्ध्वपवित्रो वाजिनीव स्वमृतमस्मि । द्रविणं सवर्चसम् । सुमेधा अमृतोक्षितः । इति त्रिशङ्कोर्वेदानुवचनम्
7.10.m: I am the mover of the tree! / My fame is like the crest of a mountain! / High and pure, like the immortal in the sun, I am glorious wealth, / of good wisdom, immortal, undecaying! / Such is the post-Vedic recitation of Triśaṅku. / [Pratīka index: aham, six.]

7.11.s: vedamanūcyācāryo'ntevāsinamanuśāsti | satyaṃ vada | dharmaṃ cara | svādhyāyānmā pramadaḥ | ācāryāya priyaṃ dhanamāhṛtya prajātantuṃ mā vyavacchethsīḥ | satyānna pramaditavyam | dharmānna pramaditavyam | kuśalānna pramaditavyam | bhūtyai na pramaditavyam | svādhyāyapravacanābhyāṃ na pramaditavyam
7.11.d: वेदमनूच्याचार्योऽन्तेवासिनमनुशास्ति । सत्यं वद । धर्मं चर । स्वाध्यायान्मा प्रमदः । आचार्याय प्रियं धनमाहृत्य प्रजातन्तुं मा व्यवच्छेथ्सीः । सत्यान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । धर्मान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । कुशलान्न प्रमदितव्यम् । भूत्यै न प्रमदितव्यम् । स्वाध्यायप्रवचनाभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम्
7.11.m: Having taught the Veda, the teacher instructs the pupil: Speak the truth. Practise dharma. Do not neglect your study. Having brought to the teacher the wealth he desires, do not cut off the thread of progeny. One should not swerve from truth. One should not swerve from dharma. One should not swerve from what is advantageous. One should not swerve from prosperity. One should not swerve from study and teaching.

7.11.s: devapitṛkāryābhyāṃ na pramaditavyam | mātṛdevo bhava | pitṛdevo bhava | ācāryadevo bhava | atithidevo bhava | yānyanavadyāni karmāṇi | tāni sevitavyāni | no itarāṇi | yānyasmākaṃ sucaritāni | tāni tvayopāsyāni
7.11.d: देवपितृकार्याभ्यां न प्रमदितव्यम् । मातृदेवो भव । पितृदेवो भव । आचार्यदेवो भव । अतिथिदेवो भव । यान्यनवद्यानि कर्माणि । तानि सेवितव्यानि । नो इतराणि । यान्यस्माकं सुचरितानि । तानि त्वयोपास्यानि
7.11.m: One should not swerve from duties to the gods and the fathers. Treat your mother as a god. Treat your father as a god. Treat your teacher as a god. Treat your guest as a god. Those deeds that are blameless, those should be cultivated, not others. Those conduct of ours that are good, those should be honoured by you,

7.11.s: no itarāṇi | ye ke cāsmacchreyāṃso brāhmaṇāḥ | teṣāṃ tvayā''sane na praśvasitavyam | śraddhayā deyam | aśraddhayā'deyam | śriyā deyam | hriyā deyam | bhiyā deyam | saṃvidā deyam | atha yadi te karmavicikithsā vā vṛttavicikithsā vā syāt
7.11.d: नो इतराणि । ये के चास्मच्छ्रेयांसो ब्राह्मणाः । तेषां त्वया'ऽसने न प्रश्वसितव्यम् । श्रद्धया देयम् । अश्रद्धयाऽदेयम् । श्रिया देयम् । ह्रिया देयम् । भिया देयम् । संविदा देयम् । अथ यदि ते कर्मविचिकिथ्सा वा वृत्तविचिकिथ्सा वा स्यात्
7.11.m: not others. And whatever brāhmaṇas are superior to us, in their presence you should not breathe forth. One should give with faith. One should not give without faith. One should give with abundance. One should give with modesty. One should give with awe. One should give with sympathy. Now, if you should have any doubt regarding action or doubt regarding conduct,

7.11.s: ye tatra brāhmaṇāḥ saṃmarśinaḥ | yuktā āyuktāḥ | alūkṣā dharmakāmāssyuḥ | yathā te tatra varterann | tathā tatra vartethāḥ | athābhyākhyāteṣu | ye tatra brāhmaṇāssaṃmarśinaḥ | yuktā āyuktāḥ | alūkṣā dharmakāmāssyuḥ | yathā te teṣu varterann | tathā teṣu vartethāḥ | eṣa ādeśaḥ | eṣa upadeśaḥ | eṣā vedopaniṣat | etadanuśāsanam | evamupāsitavyam | evamu caitadupāsyam
7.11.d: ये तत्र ब्राह्मणाः संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामास्स्युः । यथा ते तत्र वर्तेरन्न् । तथा तत्र वर्तेथाः । अथाभ्याख्यातेषु । ये तत्र ब्राह्मणास्संमर्शिनः । युक्ता आयुक्ताः । अलूक्षा धर्मकामास्स्युः । यथा ते तेषु वर्तेरन्न् । तथा तेषु वर्तेथाः । एष आदेशः । एष उपदेशः । एषा वेदोपनिषत् । एतदनुशासनम् । एवमुपासितव्यम् । एवमु चैतदुपास्यम्
7.11.m: whatever brāhmaṇas there are who are deliberative, experienced, independent, gentle, lovers of dharma—as they would conduct themselves there, so should you conduct yourself there. Then regarding those accused of blame: whatever brāhmaṇas there are who are deliberative, experienced, independent, gentle, lovers of dharma—as they would conduct themselves toward them, so should you conduct yourself toward them. This is the command. This is the instruction. This is the secret doctrine of the Veda. This is the injunction. In this way it should be worshipped. And thus, indeed, this should be revered. / [Pratīka index: svādhyāyapravacanābhyāṃ na pramaditavyam, tāni tvayopāsyāni, syāt, teṣu varteran, and seven.]

7.12.s: śaṃ no mitraḥ śaṃ varuṇaḥ | śaṃ no bhavatvaryamā | śaṃ na indro bṛhaspatiḥ | śaṃ no viṣṇururukramaḥ | namo brahmaṇe | namaste vāyo | tvameva pratyakṣaṃ brahmāsi | tvāmeva pratyakṣaṃ brahmāvādiṣam | ṛtamavādiṣam | satyamavādiṣam | tanmāmāvīt | tadvaktāramāvīt | āvīnmām | āvīdvaktāram | oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
7.12.d: शं नो मित्रः शं वरुणः । शं नो भवत्वर्यमा । शं न इन्द्रो बृहस्पतिः । शं नो विष्णुरुरुक्रमः । नमो ब्रह्मणे । नमस्ते वायो । त्वमेव प्रत्यक्षं ब्रह्मासि । त्वामेव प्रत्यक्षं ब्रह्मावादिषम् । ऋतमवादिषम् । सत्यमवादिषम् । तन्मामावीत् । तद्वक्तारमावीत् । आवीन्माम् । आवीद्वक्तारम् । ओं शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः
7.12.m:
May Mitra be auspicious to us, and Varuṇa auspicious; may Aryaman be auspicious to us; may Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us; may Viṣṇu of wide stride be auspicious to us. Homage to brahman! Homage to you, Vāyu! You alone are the directly perceived brahman. You alone have I declared as the directly perceived brahman; I have spoken the right; I have spoken truth. That has protected me; that has protected the speaker. It has protected me; it has protected the speaker. Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
[I have spoken truth, and five]
12: May [Mitra] be auspicious to us; the study; together may he [protect] us two; he who of meters; earth; that which; earth; oṃ; and right; I; having taught the Veda; may [Mitra] be auspicious to us: twelve. 12: May [Mitra] be auspicious to us; mahas; thus Āditya; not the others: twenty-three. 23: May [Mitra] be auspicious to us; peace, peace.

May Mitra be auspicious to us, and Varuṇa auspicious; may Aryaman be auspicious to us; may Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us; may Viṣṇu of wide stride be auspicious to us. Homage to brahman! Homage to you, Vāyu!
You alone are the directly perceived brahman. You alone will I declare as the directly perceived brahman; I will speak the right; I will speak truth. May that protect me; may that protect the speaker. May it protect me;
may it protect the speaker. Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!

8.1.s: brahmavidāpnoti param | tadeṣā'bhyuktā | satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma | yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ parame vyomann | so'śnute sarvānkāmānthsaha | brahmaṇā vipaściteti | tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśassaṃbhūtaḥ | ākāśādvāyuḥ | vāyoragniḥ | agnerāpaḥ | adbhyaḥ pṛthivī | pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadhībhyo'nnam | annātpuruṣaḥ | sa vā eṣa puruṣo'nnarasamayaḥ | tasyedameva śiraḥ | ayaṃ dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | ayamuttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | ayamātmā | idaṃ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.1.d: ब्रह्मविदाप्नोति परम् । तदेषाऽभ्युक्ता । सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म । यो वेद निहितं गुहायां परमे व्योमन्न् । सोऽश्नुते सर्वान्कामान्थ्सह । ब्रह्मणा विपश्चितेति । तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशस्संभूतः । आकाशाद्वायुः । वायोरग्निः । अग्नेरापः । अद्भ्यः पृथिवी । पृथिव्या ओषधयः । ओषधीभ्योऽन्नम् । अन्नात्पुरुषः । स वा एष पुरुषोऽन्नरसमयः । तस्येदमेव शिरः । अयं दक्षिणः पक्षः । अयमुत्तरः पक्षः । अयमात्मा । इदं पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति
8.1.m:
The knower of brahman attains the supreme. Concerning that, this verse is spoken:
Brahman is truth, knowledge, infinite.
He who knows it hidden in the secret place, in the highest heaven,
attains all desires together
with the wise brahman.
From that very Self, space arose;
from space, wind; from wind, fire; from fire, water; from water, earth; from earth, plants; from plants, food; from food, man. This man consists indeed of the essence of food. This is indeed his head; this is the right wing; this is the left wing; this is the trunk; this tail is the support. On that also there is this verse:

8.2.s: annādvai prajāḥ prajāyante | yāḥ kāśca pṛthivīg śritāḥ | atho annenaiva jīvanti | athainadapi yantyantataḥ | annaṃ hi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭham | tasmāthsarvauṣadhamucyate | sarvaṃ vai te'nnamāpnuvanti | ye'nnaṃ brahmopāsate | annaṃ hi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭham | tasmāthsarvauṣadhamucyate | annādbhūtāni jāyante | jātānyannena vardhante | adyate'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyata iti | tasmādvā etasmādannarasamayāt | anyo'ntara ātmā prāṇamayaḥ | tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ | sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva | tasya puruṣavidhatām | anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ | tasya prāṇa eva śiraḥ | vyāno dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | apāna uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | ākāśa ātmā | pṛthivī pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.2.d: अन्नाद्वै प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते । याः काश्च पृथिवीग् श्रिताः । अथो अन्नेनैव जीवन्ति । अथैनदपि यन्त्यन्ततः । अन्नं हि भूतानां ज्येष्ठम् । तस्माथ्सर्वौषधमुच्यते । सर्वं वै तेऽन्नमाप्नुवन्ति । येऽन्नं ब्रह्मोपासते । अन्नं हि भूतानां ज्येष्ठम् । तस्माथ्सर्वौषधमुच्यते । अन्नाद्भूतानि जायन्ते । जातान्यन्नेन वर्धन्ते । अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यत इति । तस्माद्वा एतस्मादन्नरसमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा प्राणमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य प्राण एव शिरः । व्यानो दक्षिणः पक्षः । अपान उत्तरः पक्षः । आकाश आत्मा । पृथिवी पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति

8.3.s: prāṇaṃ devā anuprāṇanti | manuṣyāḥ paśavaśca ye | prāṇo hi bhūtānāmāyuḥ | tasmāthsarvāyuṣamucyate | sarvameva ta āyuryanti | ye prāṇaṃ brahmopāsate | prāṇo hi bhūtānāmāyuḥ | tasmāthsarvāyuṣamucyata iti | tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā | yaḥ pūrvasya | tasmādvā etasmātprāṇamayāt | anyo'ntara ātmā manomayaḥ | tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ | sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva | tasya puruṣavidhatām | anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ | tasya yajureva śiraḥ | ṛgdakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | sāmottaraḥ pakṣaḥ | ādeśa ātmā | atharvāṅgirasaḥ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.3.d: प्राणं देवा अनुप्राणन्ति । मनुष्याः पशवश्च ये । प्राणो हि भूतानामायुः । तस्माथ्सर्वायुषमुच्यते । सर्वमेव त आयुर्यन्ति । ये प्राणं ब्रह्मोपासते । प्राणो हि भूतानामायुः । तस्माथ्सर्वायुषमुच्यत इति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्मात्प्राणमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा मनोमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य यजुरेव शिरः । ऋग्दक्षिणः पक्षः । सामोत्तरः पक्षः । आदेश आत्मा । अथर्वाङ्गिरसः पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति

8.4.s: yato vāco nivartante | aprāpya manasā saha | ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān | na bibheti kadācaneti | tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā | yaḥ pūrvasya | tasmādvā etasmānmanomayāt | anyo'ntara ātmā vijñānamayaḥ | tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ | sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva | tasya puruṣavidhatām | anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ | tasya śraddhaiva śiraḥ | ṛtaṃ dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | satyamuttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | yoga ātmā | mahaḥ pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.4.d: यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते । अप्राप्य मनसा सह । आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान् । न बिभेति कदाचनेति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्मान्मनोमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा विज्ञानमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य श्रद्धैव शिरः । ऋतं दक्षिणः पक्षः । सत्यमुत्तरः पक्षः । योग आत्मा । महः पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति
8.4.m:
Whence words turn back,
together with the mind, not having reached [it]—
knowing the bliss of brahman,
he fears not anything ever.
This is indeed the bodily Self of that former one. Distinct from this [Self] consisting of mind, there is another, inner Self consisting of understanding. By that, this is filled. That one is indeed shaped like a man. In accordance with its human shape, this one is shaped like a man. Its head is faith alone; the right is the right wing; truth is the left wing; yoga is the trunk; mahas is the tail, the support. On that also there is this verse:

8.5.s: vijñānaṃ yajñaṃ tanute | karmāṇi tanute'pi ca | vijñānaṃ devāssarve | brahma jyeṣṭhamupāsate | vijñānaṃ brahma cedveda | tasmāccenna pramādyati | śarīre pāpmano hitvā | sarvānkāmānthsamaśnuta iti | tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā | yaḥ pūrvasya | tasmādvā etasmādvijñānamayāt | anyo'ntara ātmā''nandamayaḥ | tenaiṣa pūrṇaḥ | sa vā eṣa puruṣavidha eva | tasya puruṣavidhatām | anvayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ | tasya priyameva śiraḥ | modo dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣaḥ | pramoda uttaraḥ pakṣaḥ | ānanda ātmā | brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.5.d: विज्ञानं यज्ञं तनुते । कर्माणि तनुतेऽपि च । विज्ञानं देवास्सर्वे । ब्रह्म ज्येष्ठमुपासते । विज्ञानं ब्रह्म चेद्वेद । तस्माच्चेन्न प्रमाद्यति । शरीरे पाप्मनो हित्वा । सर्वान्कामान्थ्समश्नुत इति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । तस्माद्वा एतस्माद्विज्ञानमयात् । अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा'ऽनन्दमयः । तेनैष पूर्णः । स वा एष पुरुषविध एव । तस्य पुरुषविधताम् । अन्वयं पुरुषविधः । तस्य प्रियमेव शिरः । मोदो दक्षिणः पक्षः । प्रमोद उत्तरः पक्षः । आनन्द आत्मा । ब्रह्म पुच्छं प्रतिष्ठा । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति
8.5.m:
Understanding extends the sacrifice,
and it extends rites as well.
Understanding do all the gods
revere as the eldest brahman.
If one knows understanding as brahman,
and does not swerve from it,
casting off sins in the body,
he attains all desires.
This is indeed the bodily Self of that former one. Distinct from this [Self] consisting of understanding, there is another, inner Self consisting of bliss.
By that, this is filled. That one is indeed shaped like a man. In accordance with its human shape, this one is shaped like a man. Its head is love alone; joy is the right wing; delight is the left wing; bliss is the trunk; brahman is the tail, the support. On that also there is this verse:

8.6.s: asanneva sa bhavati | asadbrahmeti veda cet | asti brahmeti cedveda | santamenaṃ tato viduriti | tasyaiṣa eva śārīra ātmā | yaḥ pūrvasya | athāto'nupraśnāḥ | utāvidvānamuṃ lokaṃ pretya | kaścana gacchatī | āho vidvānamuṃ lokaṃ pretya | kaścithsamaśnutāu | so'kāmayata | bahu syāṃ prajāyeyeti | sa tapo'tapyata | sa tapastaptvā | idaṃ sarvamasṛjata | yadidaṃ kiṃca | tathsṛṣṭvā | tadevānuprāviśat | tadanupraviśya | sacca tyaccābhavat | niruktaṃ cāniruktaṃ ca | nilayanaṃ cānilayanaṃ ca | vijñānaṃ cāvijñānaṃ ca | satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca satyamabhavat | yadidaṃ kiṃca | tathsatyamityācakṣate | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.6.d: असन्नेव स भवति । असद्ब्रह्मेति वेद चेत् । अस्ति ब्रह्मेति चेद्वेद । सन्तमेनं ततो विदुरिति । तस्यैष एव शारीर आत्मा । यः पूर्वस्य । अथातोऽनुप्रश्नाः । उताविद्वानमुं लोकं प्रेत्य । कश्चन गच्छती । आहो विद्वानमुं लोकं प्रेत्य । कश्चिथ्समश्नुताउ । सोऽकामयत । बहु स्यां प्रजायेयेति । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्त्वा । इदं सर्वमसृजत । यदिदं किंच । तथ्सृष्ट्वा । तदेवानुप्राविशत् । तदनुप्रविश्य । सच्च त्यच्चाभवत् । निरुक्तं चानिरुक्तं च । निलयनं चानिलयनं च । विज्ञानं चाविज्ञानं च । सत्यं चानृतं च सत्यमभवत् । यदिदं किंच । तथ्सत्यमित्याचक्षते । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति
8.6.m:
He becomes non-existent indeed,
if he knows brahman as non-existent.
If he knows that brahman is,
then they know him as existing.
This is indeed the bodily Self of that former one.
Now, then, follow questions: Does any non-knower, on departing, go to yonder world? Or does any knower, on departing, attain yonder world? He desired: "May I be many, may I be born." He performed ascetic heat. Having performed ascetic heat, he emitted all this, whatever there is here. Having emitted it, he entered into that very thing. Having entered into it,
he became the actual and the beyond, the defined and the undefined, the rooted and the rootless, understanding and non-understanding, truth and falsehood: the truth became [all this], whatever there is here. That they call truth. On that also there is this verse:

8.7.s: asadvā idamagra āsīt | tato vai sadajāyata | tadātmānaṃ svayamakuruta | tasmāttathsukṛtamucyata iti | yadvai tathsukṛtam | raso vai saḥ | rasaṃ hyevāyaṃ labdhvā''nandī bhavati | ko hyevānyātkaḥ prāṇyāt | yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāt | eṣa hyevā''nandayāti | yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnadṛśye'nātmye'nirukte'nilayane'bhayaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vindate | atha so'bhayaṃ gato bhavati | yadā hyevaiṣa etasminnudaramantaraṃ kurute | atha tasya bhayaṃ bhavati | tattveva bhayaṃ viduṣo'manvānasya | tadapyeṣa śloko bhavati
8.7.d: असद्वा इदमग्र आसीत् । ततो वै सदजायत । तदात्मानं स्वयमकुरुत । तस्मात्तथ्सुकृतमुच्यत इति । यद्वै तथ्सुकृतम् । रसो वै सः । रसं ह्येवायं लब्ध्वा'ऽनन्दी भवति । को ह्येवान्यात्कः प्राण्यात् । यदेष आकाश आनन्दो न स्यात् । एष ह्येवा'ऽनन्दयाति । यदा ह्येवैष एतस्मिन्नदृश्येऽनात्म्येऽनिरुक्तेऽनिलयनेऽभयं प्रतिष्ठां विन्दते । अथ सोऽभयं गतो भवति । यदा ह्येवैष एतस्मिन्नुदरमन्तरं कुरुते । अथ तस्य भयं भवति । तत्त्वेव भयं विदुषोऽमन्वानस्य । तदप्येष श्लोको भवति
8.7.m: "Non-being, truly, was this in the beginning; / From that, indeed, being was born. / That made itself by itself; / Therefore, it is called well-made." / That which is well-made, that indeed is the essence. Having obtained that essence, one becomes blissful. For who indeed would breathe out, who would breathe in, if this space were not bliss? For he alone causes bliss. When indeed he finds fearless standing in this invisible, bodiless, unexpressed, unhoused [brahman], then he has attained fearlessness. When, however, he makes even the slightest difference in it, then fear arises for him. That indeed is the fear of the wise man who does not reflect. On that too there is this verse:
